records.name: Alleles, zygosity and copy state
records.tldr: An allele is a sequence version at a genomic location. Which versions are present and how many DNA copies exist are separate questions.
records.summary: At a diploid location, heterozygous means that the two copies differ in the feature being considered; homozygous means they match. Hemizygous describes a single copy in the specified context. Tumor gains, losses and genome doubling can make a two-copy model inadequate. Loss of heterozygosity means loss of previously different allelic information; it can accompany a deletion or occur while total copy count remains unchanged. Total copy number alone cannot identify which allele was retained.

notes: Variant allele frequency counts supporting reads or molecules under the assay’s definition. Purity, local copy state, subclonal mixtures and method affect it; it is not directly a cancer-cell percentage or a zygosity call. Phase asks whether specified variants share a DNA copy, a further question that a gene-name match does not answer.

Biallelic inactivation concerns whether either parental contribution still supplies useful function in the relevant cancer-cell population, rather than simply counting two physical DNA copies or two events somewhere in a tissue. A damaging change plus loss of the other contribution can support it, but phasing, allele-specific copy state, consequence and cell mixture matter. High VAF alone cannot establish this state. Nguyen and colleagues' pan-cancer analysis associated particular biallelic repair-gene alterations with genomic damage patterns; that association does not make every variant in every repair gene functionally equivalent or establish present drug sensitivity.

A haplotype groups linked sequence variants on a chromosome that tend to be inherited together. Phasing assigns variants to chromosome copies; that is different from counting carrier cancer cells. Labels A and B distinguish sequence versions without grading either as harmful or harmless. In a fictional set of 100 cancer cells, two variants each present in forty cells could occupy the same forty or separate groups of forty. The two individual fractions do not reveal their overlap. Joint sequence or cell-resolved evidence addresses co-occurrence, with its own sampling limits. Neither shared prevalence nor physical phase alone establishes a variant's functional importance.

records.name: Analytical versus clinical validation
records.tldr: Analytical validity concerns whether a test measures reliably. Clinical validity concerns what its result means for a condition or outcome. Clinical utility concerns using that information for a decision.
records.summary: Analytical validity, clinical validity and clinical utility address different questions for a specified assay, specimen, population and intended use. MedlinePlus Genetics distinguishes detection of a genetic variant, its relationship to disease presence or risk, and whether the information helps diagnosis, treatment, management or prevention. Reliable measurement does not by itself establish clinical meaning, and an outcome association does not establish benefit from changing care. For a prediction model, reproducibility of fixed-input output, discrimination, calibrated probabilities and the consequences of model-guided decisions also require distinct evidence. These are related questions rather than a universal sequence that guarantees a useful test.

notes: Start a claim worksheet with the population and treatment setting, specimen and method version, measured or predicted outcome, time horizon and proposed decision. A molecule measurement, drug ranking in a dish and outcome prediction from earlier patients are different claims. For risk, retain whether the estimate assumes usual care or no treatment; for a drug experiment, retain the drug, dose and combination. Leave unavailable details unknown. Then separate the tested material and quality, biological interpretation and alternatives, prediction, proposed action and evidence of benefit. Mark each measured, inferred, proposed or unknown. A sound measurement does not automatically support the later steps.

Consider a fictional report that calls a protein-rich stored tumour a Drug A responder. Its study related protein abundance to shrinkage among people all receiving Drug A for advanced Cancer X. The measurement and response association can be useful, but there is no untreated or alternative-treatment comparison establishing greater benefit from A. Applying it after surgery also changes the setting. Ask what comparison shows improved outcomes from choosing A with this result in the proposed setting. Confirmation of protein abundance answers whether that signal is real, while postoperative benefit remains a separate question. A favourable prognostic result does not itself justify omitting standard treatment.

An evidence card records population, stage, treatment context and selection; specimen, handling, assay version and quality criteria; the reference condition or care comparator and its limitations; outcome and measurement time; the analysis plan, all tuning and independent evaluation; failed samples, dropout and missing outcomes; and sample size, intervals and remaining uncertainty. A response endpoint is not recurrence or survival. A preclinical card names the actual model and tested claim; an observational clinical association retains possible confounding. Neither alone establishes that the proposed clinical action helps. A headline metric also needs the consequences of false positive and false negative calls attached to the action. Distinguish prespecified analyses from exploratory searches, keep their tuning history, and seek confirmation that does not reuse the search. State whether a treatment-study denominator includes everyone assigned, only those treated or only those evaluable.

For analytical performance, request the detection limit with its target level, input amount, specimen and detection probability; precision within runs and across days, operators, instruments and reagent lots; agreement with an appropriate independent reference; attempted-sample failure rate and reasons; and specimen handling, preservation and interference testing. The 2017 AMP/CAP recommendations concern next-generation sequencing panels for somatic variants. They ask for performance by variant class and relevant reference materials, depth and sample numbers. They describe a lower detection limit at which 95 per cent of samples are reliably detected, but also explain why observing 19 or 20 successes in 20 trials does not by itself establish that reliability with confidence. This is an assay-specific example, not a universal validation protocol. Fresh and delayed specimens can differ, and measurement variation must be understood before interpreting a trend. Self-agreement alone does not establish accuracy.

Put the decision before ordering. Write what positive, negative, uncertain and failed results would change, including proposed treatment omission, confirmation or another sample. Compare existing pathology and other tests, and record the decision deadline, finite tissue, time, travel, uncertainty and financial burden. Name who interprets the result, who owns the clinical recommendation and when further testing is unlikely to help that decision. A result arriving after the decision closes may not serve its intended use. The worksheet exposes assumptions rather than calculating a treatment choice; urgency does not establish validity.

In the fictional postoperative protein-test case, possible next steps are checking the actual companion-diagnostic requirement and whether this assay meets it, inspecting the Drug A evidence, considering a trial of the relevant strategy, or declining a tissue-consuming test that would not change the decision. The exact laboratory, service, version and intended use matter. A research-use label, laboratory certification, development designation or report drug list cannot replace the claim-specific evidence. A companion test is tied to specified treatment use. Clinician-led off-label use, access, payment and suitability are additional questions, not promises made by a molecular report. Fast-track and breakthrough-therapy designations are not marketing approval; accelerated approval is a distinct approval pathway, not just a development designation.

Research can have a defined value without selecting treatment: checking a mechanism, explaining discordant assays or generating a future hypothesis. Name the reviewer and what would count as a useful answer rather than extending an endless chain of tests. Attribute unpublished company data and state which methods and results were available to inspect; unavailable evidence does not prove the claim false. In a fictional high/low recurrence-risk test for which neither answer changes recommended care and no relevant study is open, the immediate value for that treatment decision is limited. A separate research or personal-information goal should be weighed against burden, uncertainty and alternatives. A changed treatment decision is not itself demonstrated benefit and can add unnecessary treatment.

records.name: Antibody
records.tldr: A typical IgG antibody has antigen-binding arms and a stem that can interact with other parts of the immune system. Binding alone does not specify its function.
records.summary: A typical IgG has two antigen-binding arms; receptor binding and cross-reactivity depend on the particular molecule and test system, while its stem (the Fc region) can recruit immune cells and complement or extend the antibody's life in the blood. Therapeutic antibodies block growth receptors (trastuzumab on HER2, cetuximab on EGFR), release the brakes on T cells (pembrolizumab on PD-1), flag cancer cells for immune killing (rituximab on CD20), or serve as the targeting vehicle of ADCs and radioimmunotherapy. Bispecific formats have two binding specificities. Some are designed to bring a T cell and a target cell together; their structures and functions vary. Fab, the arm with the binding site, and Fc, the stem, are separate parts: binding does not guarantee killing, and Fc effector contacts need compatible effector cells or complement. Antibodies that bind the same target can act differently: a blocking antibody, an antibody-drug conjugate and a bispecific format can share a target and still differ in what follows.

records.name: B2M
records.tldr: B2M supplies a light-chain protein used by class I HLA and several related complexes. A variant or RNA result alone does not establish loss of these functions.
records.summary:
Component of the class I major histocompatibility complex (MHC). Involved in the presentation of peptide antigens to the immune system. Exogenously applied M.tuberculosis EsxA or EsxA-EsxB (or EsxA expressed in host) binds B2M and decreases its export to the cell surface (total protein levels do not change), probably leading to defects in class I antigen presentation.

CIViC holds 7 clinical evidence items and 0 assertions across 4 variants, naming Pembrolizumab, Nivolumab, Anti-PD-L1 Monoclonal Antibody and Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor and others. Open Targets scores its association with cancer at 0.69 (direct and indirect evidence; datatypes literature 0.98, affected pathway 0.61, genetic association 0.00, somatic mutation 0.88). IntOGen calls it a driver in 10 cohorts (4 activating, 6 loss-of-function), covering Cervical Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma, NOS, Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Melanoma, Malignant Lymphoma, Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma and others.

Roles: CIViC lists 5 therapies; IntOGen calls it an activating (Act) driver in 4 cohorts; IntOGen calls it a loss-of-function (LoF) driver in 6 cohorts; CIViC holds 7 clinical evidence items on its variants. Evidence tier "clinical-evidence" is the strongest of those signals.
Prevalence not recorded: none of the sources gives a positivity rate.

Colorectal cancer: inactivating mutation in 3 to 7% overall but 31.0% of MSI-high against 1.5% of microsatellite-stable samples in crc_msk_2026, with biallelic B2M and HLA loss by copy-number change and copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity documented across 1,211 tumours (Grasso 2018). It is an immunoediting scar and the best available explanation for the mismatch repair deficient patients who do not respond to a checkpoint inhibitor.

Lymphoma, RHOA G17V and the epigenetic mutations of T-follicular-helper lymphoma: A single substitution, G17V, in the small GTPase RHOA produces a protein that does not bind GTP and that blocks the wild-type protein as well. It is specific to the tumour cell, whereas the TET2 mutations that accompany it are found in non-tumour haematopoietic cells too, which places the TET2 lesion earlier, in the stem cell, and makes this lymphoma a disease that grows out of clonal haematopoiesis. Frequency: RHOA G17V in 68% of angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma samples, with every G17V case also carrying a TET2 mutation (Sakata-Yanagimoto 2014); independently, in 22 of 35 angioimmunoblastic cases, 67%, and 8 of 44 peripheral T-cell lymphoma not otherwise specified, 18%, alongside recurrent TET2, DNMT3A and IDH2 mutations and less frequent FYN, ATM, B2M and CD58 lesions (Palomero 2014). What it changes about treatment: Not through an approved test. The hypomethylating agents are used in this disease on the strength of the TET2 and DNMT3A biology rather than on a mutation result, and azacitidine-containing regimens have shown activity in T-follicular-helper histology specifically.

Teaching distinction from the antigen-antibodies audit (9 November 2026): B2M is the class I light chain and not part of class II; loss of functional B2M affects many class I targets, unlike loss of one HLA allele; B2M also partners HLA-E, HLA-G, HLA-F, MR1 and (via Wani 2006) FcRn. See the hla record.

records.name: Basal-like breast cancer
records.tldr: Basal-like describes a breast-cancer gene-expression pattern. It overlaps with receptor-defined triple-negative disease, but the labels use different measurements and are not interchangeable.
records.summary: Perou and colleagues profiled 65 surgical specimens from 42 patients on cDNA microarrays of 8,102 genes and found the tumours could be classified into subtypes distinguished by pervasive differences in gene expression, the origin of the intrinsic subtypes luminal A, luminal B, HER2-enriched, basal-like and normal-like (Perou 2000). The Cancer Genome Atlas integrated copy number, methylation, exome, mRNA, microRNA and protein data across primary breast cancers, confirmed four main classes, found TP53, PIK3CA and GATA3 the only genes mutated in more than 10 percent overall, and showed basal-like tumours share many molecular features with high-grade serous ovarian cancer, implying a related aetiology and similar therapeutic opportunities (TCGA 2012). Triple-negative and basal-like overlap but are not identical: of 412 triple-negative tumours 21.4 percent were non-basal-like, and of 473 basal-like tumours 31.5 percent were not triple-negative; triple-negative tumours classified as luminal or HER2-enriched had expression profiles indistinguishable from their non-triple-negative counterparts, most HER2-enriched triple-negative tumours lacked HER2 amplification, and the authors suggest triple-negative trials stratify by basal-like versus non-basal-like expression (Prat 2013). In the population-based Carolina Breast Cancer Study, using immunohistochemical surrogates (ER, PR and HER2 negative with cytokeratin 5/6 or HER1 positive), basal-like tumours were found in 39 percent of premenopausal African American women against 14 percent of postmenopausal African American and 16 percent of non-African American women; they had more TP53 mutations (44 against 15 percent), higher mitotic index and grade, and among the shortest breast cancer-specific survival (Carey 2006). Basal-like cancers are the typical cancer of BRCA1 carriers, and adenoid cystic carcinoma is a special type of basal-like tumour with an excellent outlook (Ghabach 2010), a reminder that an expression label does not establish a uniform behaviour or exact cell ancestry. PAM50 basal-like and Lehmann BL1/BL2 belong to different classifiers; a PAM50 basal-like call does not by itself assign either Lehmann profile.

notes: A research expression label, a receptor-test classification, a histological type and an inherited-risk result describe different observations. Keep the specimen, classifier/version, preprocessing, reference data and uncertainty. A label or pathway-enrichment pattern alone does not establish functional dependence or benefit from a particular treatment.

A normal-like or basal-like classifier output is not a diagnosis of benign tissue or proof of origin in a mature basal cell. The research classifier, receptor tests and histology remain separately interpretable.

Basal-marker immunohistochemistry provides contextual protein evidence, not a stand-alone subtype from ribonucleic acid (RNA) or an exact lineage trace. SOX10 is the gene symbol for SRY-box transcription factor 10; the encoded protein is a transcription factor whose tissue assay commonly assesses nuclear signal. CK5/6 denotes cytokeratins 5 and 6, epithelial structural proteins, while EGFR means epidermal growth factor receptor and is also called HER1. Nielsen and colleagues evaluated an ER, HER2, CK5/6 and EGFR protein surrogate against expression-defined basal-like cancers and in a historical tissue series. A specified research panel is not equivalent to one marker reproducing a full RNA classifier.

Cimino-Mathews and colleagues found SOX10 nuclear staining in normal myoepithelial cells and in a subset of selected triple-negative and metaplastic breast carcinomas. Their series had 100 invasive cancers, with 38 of 58 basal-like, unclassified TNBC or metaplastic cases staining, compared with two of 42 luminal/HER2 cases. These selected-series frequencies are not universal prevalence or diagnostic sensitivity. SOX10 also occurs in other tumours, including melanoma and peripheral nerve-sheath tumours. Positive staining alone does not prove breast origin, and a negative result does not exclude breast carcinoma.

Ask which cells carry the signal before interpreting a stain. Two fictional sketches can show SOX10-positive nuclei in benign myoepithelial cells around a duct and in a separate malignant-cell region. They are illustrations, not micrographs, positivity cutoffs or proof from anatomy alone. In a fictional axillary SOX10-positive mass, identify the intended cells and localisation, morphology, other markers and clinical context before assigning an origin. SOX10 does not by itself establish breast origin, basal-like RNA, Lehmann BL1, ancestry, treatment dependence or vaccine benefit.

A stain report needs the tissue/lesion and selected cells, fixation, antibody and protocol, nuclear or other expected localisation, scoring rule, presence, intensity and percentage among the intended cells. Appropriate positive and negative controls, including interpretable internal tissue controls, are needed. Preservation, scant tumour, background and staining of neighbouring benign cells can limit interpretation. Protein presence is not direct transcription-factor activity, an RNA classifier, lineage tracing or a drug-response assay. The percentage of stained tumour cells is not the probability that a treatment will work. Associations with outcome in a tissue cohort do not establish added benefit from a treatment.

records.name: BH3 profiling (functional apoptosis testing)
records.tldr: BH3 profiling measures mitochondrial responses to defined challenges in sampled cells to investigate readiness for apoptosis and survival dependencies.
records.summary: BH3 profiling challenges the mitochondrial apoptosis system of viable sampled cells using defined peptides after selective plasma-membrane permeabilisation. Protocols read mitochondrial depolarisation or cytochrome-c loss. Baseline priming and dependence patterns differ from the change after a named drug exposure in dynamic profiling. Published experiments link early priming changes with later cytotoxic responses in their studied models and samples; this does not establish a universal companion diagnostic or treatment-selection rule.

notes: Assay card. Input: viable single-cell suspension from tissue, blood or a suitable model, with cell identity and population gating documented. Routine fixed archival tissue cannot supply the starting living cells. Permeabilisation and peptide challenge consume the tested aliquots; cell demand depends on panel, controls and replicates rather than one universal tissue minimum. Output: named peptide response, dose, exposure time and population, reported as protocol-normalised depolarisation or cytochrome-c loss. Drug-minus-vehicle delta priming is in percentage points. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymeth.2013.04.006 ; https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4939-8861-7_4

Normalisation and failure checks. In the Ryan and Letai potential-dye protocol, vehicle and a depolarising control define the assay range: subtract the depolarising-control signal from the sample and vehicle signals. Divide the sample difference by the vehicle difference, subtract that ratio from one and multiply by 100 to obtain percent depolarisation. This is not an absolute percentage of dead cells. In cytochrome-c protocols, read retained or lost signal against the specified controls and gating convention; do not interchange fluorescence retention and release. Poor baseline viability, damaged mitochondria, excessive permeabilisation, wrong cell identity, loss of tumour populations or saturated responses can invalidate comparison. Thresholds are protocol- and study-specific. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymeth.2013.04.006 ; https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4939-8861-7_4

Reading rule. State measured priming, separately measured later death and clinical outcome independently. An early drug-induced priming change can precede detectable killing; it neither identifies a causal variant nor establishes achievable exposure, systemic toxicity or benefit for another population. Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2015.01.042

BH3 means BCL-2 homology 3. BAX and BAK can permeabilise the mitochondrial outer membrane, releasing cytochrome c from between the mitochondrial membranes into the cytosol. Priming concerns proximity to that threshold, not merely protein abundance. HRK-derived peptide preferentially probes BCL-XL, while BAD-derived peptide also challenges BCL-2 and BCL-W; overlapping patterns and concentrations matter. The assay peptide is not a vaccine-antigen recognition test. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/bjc.2016.49

BCL-2, BCL-XL and MCL-1 oppose apoptosis, whereas other family members promote it; a BH3 region is a protein region participating in this signalling. A larger mitochondrial response to the same defined challenge can indicate greater priming, and cytochrome-c release helps initiate downstream death machinery. Strong protein staining alone does not establish functional dependence. Butterworth compared peptide profiles with selective BH3-mimetic inhibitors: using both was more informative when survival involved multiple anti-apoptotic proteins, so discordant readouts warrant investigation. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/bjc.2016.49

In a fictional dynamic-profiling experiment, cells pre-exposed to vehicle show 20 percent normalised depolarisation when given a peptide, and cells pre-exposed to the drug show 55 percent for the same peptide. (In the normalisation, peptide-free vehicle wells define 0 percent and the depolarising control defines 100 percent; the 20 percent belongs to vehicle-pre-exposed cells challenged with the peptide.) The increase is 35 percentage points, not a 35 percent killed-cell fraction, a causal variant finding or a safe treatment. Values can exceed 100 percent in the potential-dye protocol, so the scale must not be read as a literal cell-death fraction. Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymeth.2013.04.006
records.principle: Compare mitochondrial responses to defined peptide challenges with protocol-specific controls; dynamic profiling compares drug-treated with vehicle-treated cells.
strengths: Functional measurement of mitochondrial apoptotic readiness
Can investigate response patterns across survival proteins
limitations: Requires viable identified cells and adequate control separation
Peptide specificity overlaps; a single response may not identify one dependency
Priming is separate from intact-cell killing and patient benefit

records.name: Bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and the full transcriptome
records.tldr: Bulk RNA sequencing measures captured messages pooled across a tissue sample, including contributions from multiple cell types.
records.summary: RNA carries cellular messages; bulk sequencing samples those messages from combined tissue after protocol-specific capture and preparation. Analysis assigns usable observations to genes or transcripts and applies a defined comparison scale. A change can reflect cell composition, expression within cells or both. Gene totals can conceal transcript differences, and pooled RNA does not directly establish protein localisation, pathway flux or drug dependence.

notes: Bulk RNA sequencing measures captured messages pooled across a specimen. Cancer, immune and supporting cells can contribute different amounts of RNA; a higher signal can reflect a changed mixture, changed expression within cells, or both. Zero detected reads does not establish biological absence. Source: Conesa et al., 2016 methods review, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-016-0881-8.

Name the counting unit and normalisation denominator. Estimated transcript counts, length-adjusted transcripts per million and tagged molecule counts answer different measurement questions. A gene total can conceal splice products; pooled RNA does not directly measure surface protein, pathway flux or drug dependence. Sources: https://salmon.readthedocs.io/en/latest/file_formats.html and https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-016-0881-8.

Fictional mixture exercise: in two 100-cell samples, increasing identical marker-producing lymphocytes from 20 to 40 doubles their stipulated marker molecules if each contributes one and other cells contribute none. This does not show cancer-cell activation. Equal RNA contribution and matched recovery are assumptions, not measured tissue properties.
Bulk RNA-seq extracts RNA, prepares a library (often cDNA), may select mRNA or deplete rRNA or capture regions; bulk does not mean equal capture of all molecules.
Reads or fragments are assigned to genes or transcripts; shared sequences make assignment ambiguous; a count table is already shaped by preparation and analysis.
A bulk signal can rise because more cells of a type contribute, expression within them rises, or both; deconvolution estimates contributions under a model and does not separate cells.
Gene-level counts can hide isoform differences; a mutant or splice product needs sequence or junction evidence.

Bulk RNA can nominate expressed targets and summarise programmes but does not establish cell origin, surface protein, pathway flux or drug dependence; zero reads is not absence; thousands of genes from one biopsy are not thousands of patients.

Fictional teaching exercise: With equal RNA per cell, a lymphocyte-only marker and 100-cell pieces, raising lymphocytes from 20 to 40 doubles the pooled marker (20 to 40 stipulated molecules) without changing any cancer cell.
Record sampled region and RNA integrity; research profiling differs from a validated clinical RNA test.

Record protocol-compatible preservation, sampled region, RNA integrity and material consumed by extraction. Track capture, sequence assignment, read/fragment units, normalisation and transcript calls. Preparation time varies; reference material, process controls and biological replicates test different uncertainties. Degradation, contamination, ambiguous annotation, batch and mixture shifts constrain purpose-specific cutoffs and clinical intended-use validation.

A larger raw count can be a smaller share of a library. In an invented example, ten captured counts out of 10,000 give 1,000 counts per million, while twenty out of 100,000 give 200. Keep the counted unit and library-size definition. Counts per million scale by that denominator; transcripts per million also use transcript-length information under the chosen quantification method. These relative scales are not interchangeable, do not recover the total RNA made per cell and are not protein counts. A base-two log fold change of plus one corresponds to a ratio of two, and plus two to four under the stated normalization. A reference near zero can make a ratio large while the underlying signal remains small; these are mathematical examples, not biological cutoffs.

records.name: Cell lineage, identity and state
records.tldr: A cell’s ancestry, its type and its current activity answer different questions. Similar activity does not prove that two cells share a recent ancestor.
records.summary: Lineage describes descent from earlier cells. A cell type or identity describes a differentiated family, while a state describes context-dependent features such as activation, stress or cycling. A genetic clone has shared ancestry and can be tracked through specified genomic features; an RNA cluster alone does not establish that ancestry. Stem cells can renew and generate descendants; progenitor potential is restricted by the biological context. Differentiation develops specialized properties without requiring every change of state to become a new lineage.

notes: Reference atlases classify measured features. Barcodes or other validated tracing information add ancestry evidence, with their own labeling and sampling limits. Weinreb and colleagues combined expressed barcodes and transcriptomes over time in hematopoiesis; sister-cell analyses exposed fate biases that a single RNA snapshot missed. This does not identify an individual tumor’s origin from its expression profile.

Lim and colleagues studied normal and preneoplastic breast tissue from BRCA1 mutation carriers and found an expanded luminal-progenitor population. The expression profiles of BRCA1-associated tissue and basal breast tumours resembled normal luminal progenitors more than the other tested subsets. This supported a candidate population for transformation; it was not direct lineage tracing of an individual tumour. A luminal-progenitor-like RNA program does not by itself make a cancer hormone-receptor-positive.

Support a malignant-cell assignment with tissue context, a coherent marker panel, suitable normal references and quality checks, rather than one marker or cluster name. In five primary glioblastomas, Patel and colleagues profiled 430 cells and inferred broad chromosome alterations by averaging RNA expression along chromosomes against normal reference profiles. This was RNA-based inference, not a direct DNA copy count or a breast diagnostic rule. A flat inferred profile can miss a malignant cell lacking a detectable broad change; focal alterations and point mutations can also be missed. Matched DNA, pathology and spatial evidence can corroborate an assignment, but bulk DNA does not identify every RNA barcode. Mixed markers may reflect ambient RNA or doublets. In another fictional mixed sample, vimentin RNA could come from fibroblasts or a changed cancer-cell programme. Even cell-attributed expression of that marker alone does not establish invasion, resistance or ancestry. Keep uncertain assignments uncertain.

records.name: Central dogma and molecular information flow
records.tldr: DNA copying, making RNA and making a protein are different processes. Following the route helps identify what each molecular test actually measured.
records.summary: Replication makes DNA from DNA. Transcription uses a DNA template to make RNA. Translation reads the coding sequence of a message in three-base codons to build a polypeptide; the transcript and reading frame matter. Functional noncoding RNAs do not need to become protein. Reverse transcription copies RNA into DNA in relevant viral and retrotransposon contexts. This information-flow map is not a guarantee that every DNA change produces a measured RNA or protein change.

links.label: NHGRI: RNA, coding/noncoding functions and reverse transcription
NHGRI: codon
NHGRI: transcription
OpenStax: regulation across molecular steps

notes: RNA processing, translation, folding, modification, localization and turnover can alter the path from a coding sequence to a functional product. DNA presence, RNA abundance, intact protein, location and activity require their own evidence. Neither a gene-level RNA count nor a sequence prediction establishes a fixed protein amount or clinical effect.

records.name: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA)
records.tldr: Cell-free DNA is DNA outside intact cells in a collected sample. Tumour-derived DNA is one possible part of that mixture; its amount depends on the specimen and method.
records.summary:
Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is DNA outside intact cells in a specimen. Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) is the tumour-derived part of the plasma DNA mixture, rather than a different material competing with cfDNA. DNA from non-tumour tissues can contribute much of that mixture, as illustrated by Moss and colleagues' methylation-atlas study. Total extracted DNA is therefore not a tumour measurement. A finite evaluated aliquot can contain no qualifying tumour signal even when disease exists elsewhere.

Liquid biopsy describes a specimen approach. A test may track known tumour features, look for predefined mutation, methylation or fragment patterns, or profile detectable alterations. Its target coverage, origin checks, sample requirements and calling rule determine the claim. Genotyping, residual-disease monitoring and screening have different intended uses; a method label does not validate every use or locate the source of a plasma signal.

links.label: Wikipedia
Comprehensive human cell-type methylation atlas reveals origins of circulating cell-free DNA in health and disease
Maternal Plasma DNA Sequencing Reveals the Genome-Wide Genetic and Mutational Profile of the Fetus
Enhanced detection of circulating tumor DNA by fragment size analysis
Comparison of tumor‐informed and tumor‐naïve sequencing assays for ctDNA detection in breast cancer
NCI: cfDNA biospecimen collection and processing (revision February 2025)
FDA: ctDNA for curative-intent solid tumour drug development (November 2024)

notes: Source classes: cfDNA is DNA outside intact cells in a sample, and ctDNA is the tumour-derived part of that pool, so the two are related materials and not rival tests. In healthy donors a methylation atlas of 25 tissues and cell types attributed plasma cfDNA to white blood cells (55%), erythrocyte progenitors (30%), vascular endothelial cells (10%) and hepatocytes (1%) (Moss 2018). A tumour adds DNA only when it contributes, and the tumour share may be small or absent in the sample drawn even when cancer exists elsewhere.

Scale: plasma DNA fragments show a pattern reminiscent of nuclease-cleaved nucleosomes with a peak at 166 base pairs (Lo 2010, in maternal plasma), and tumour-derived fragments are enriched at 90 to 150 base pairs (Mouliere 2018). One assay input in a breast-cancer comparison was 4,500 amplifiable copies, about 15 nanograms (Santonja 2023), and at about 3.3 picograms per haploid genome copy 1 nanogram is roughly 300 copies (arithmetic from genome size). In a fictional single-locus model with 4,500 amplifiable opportunities and target-allele probability 1 in 100,000, the expected target count is 0.045. The target-allele probability is not automatically a tumour-DNA fraction: copy number, variant multiplicity and clone representation matter.

Yield is not origin: in a fictional experiment equal 1 mL plasma aliquots give 2 and 4 nanograms of cfDNA and no tumour-attributed signal is reported. Total DNA doubled, but tumour fraction and any tumour-DNA fold change cannot be calculated because tumour attribution was not measured. A fragment's source needs evidence such as paired white-blood-cell and tumour sequencing (Razavi 2019), and a variant seen in plasma is not automatically tumour-derived.

Method card: measures selected features of plasma DNA by a stated sequencing or molecular method, from a finite plasma aliquot that testing consumes. Output is detected or not detected, variant fractions, molecule concentrations or model estimates, each with its own unit. It cannot give an all-body cell count, lesion location, viability or treatment benefit, and validity belongs to the exact specimen, assay version and intended use.

Collection conditions can change the mixture before testing: blood-cell breakdown adds genomic DNA and can dilute a tumour fraction. The NCI biospecimen practices document, revised February 2025, prefers plasma to serum. Its protocol recommends EDTA, accepts acid citrate dextrose, and advises avoiding heparin and citrate; the literature-summary section separately reports results with several anticoagulants when processing was immediate. For EDTA blood the protocol prefers centrifugation within 2 hours and accepts up to 4 hours at room temperature or 24 hours at 4 degrees Celsius; it recommends stabilising tubes for anticipated delays over 2 hours. These are recommendations for that specimen workflow, not a universal acceptance rule for every assay. Extraction and library preparation then retain only some available molecules, so the volume drawn is not the volume evaluated.

Reading an assay report starts with the specimen and collection date, the plasma volume actually evaluated, DNA quality and recovery, origin checks, and the rule that turns a signal into a call. Low shedding, damaged input or failed quality controls can limit interpretation; a failed assay is a separate result from no qualifying signal. Genotyping, response monitoring and residual-disease detection are different intended uses. In its November 2024 drug-development guidance, FDA asks for validation of the complete workflow, representative clinical samples, the input range and prespecified calling cut-offs; validation of one use does not establish another.

A useful result ledger keeps six questions together: when the sample was collected and where that date sits relative to treatment or surgery; the assay and version; the specimen, evaluated input and quality qualifications; the reported state, including detected, not detected, indeterminate or failed; the quantity, unit and numerical qualifications; and the applicable detection and quantitation criteria. Keep the report-release date separately. Two reports arriving together may describe different biological moments, and an invalid sample or failed reference build is not a negative plasma result.

In a fictional comparison, one assay reports not detected and another reports a low detected signal. That alone does not identify an erroneous test. Compare the actual samples and collection dates, targets, input, controls and calling criteria before interpreting the disagreement. A valid negative says that the evaluated sample did not meet that method's qualifying-signal rule. It cannot distinguish every possibility: there may be no residual tumour signal, too few relevant fragments may have reached the aliquot, or the tracked features may not represent the remaining cells. This reading exercise sets no repeat-draw schedule.

records.name: Clonal evolution and branching models
records.tldr: Peter Nowell's 1976 idea that a tumour is an evolving population of competing clones is now measured directly by sequencing several regions or repeated blood samples, and models of branching evolution predict which clones will drive relapse.
records.summary: Nowell proposed that tumours arise from a single cell and evolve by mutation and selection into a branching tree of clones. Multi-region sequencing (TRACERx in lung cancer, from 2017) and longitudinal circulating tumour DNA confirmed branched evolution, showed truncal versus subclonal mutations, and revealed that some tumours evolve neutrally while others show strong selective sweeps. Models built on these data estimate mutation rates, timing of metastasis and the likelihood that a subclone carries resistance, and inform which mutations to target (truncal) and how to read residual disease.

links.label: Nowell 1976, Science
TRACERx, Jamal-Hanjani 2017
PyClone: statistical inference of clonal population structure in cancer (Nature methods 2014)

notes: Roth and colleagues described PyClone as a Bayesian method that groups deeply sequenced somatic mutations into putative clonal clusters while estimating cellular prevalence and accounting for copy-number imbalance and normal-cell contamination. The groups remain model-derived hypotheses about populations, rather than a direct census or a guaranteed family tree. Similar estimated prevalence alone does not show that two variants occur in the same cells, and one sampled region does not map every lesion or establish that a shared variant matters functionally.
records.principle: A tumour is a population under mutation, drift and selection; phylogenetic and branching-process models reconstruct its history from the variant allele frequencies observed across regions and time.
strengths: Directly supported by multi-region and serial sequencing
Distinguishes truncal from subclonal targets
Quantifies intratumour heterogeneity
limitations: Sampling misses small clones
Neutral versus selected evolution is debated
Costly to measure in routine care

records.name: Clonal haematopoiesis (CHIP)
records.tldr: Some blood-forming cells acquire mutations and form an expanding clone. This can affect blood tests for tumour DNA and is distinct from a diagnosis of leukaemia.
records.summary: Clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP, a defined category within blood-cell clonal expansion; see the source-specific variant-fraction and clinical criteria below) is present in >10% of people over 70. It confers ~0.5-1%/year progression to myeloid neoplasm, doubles cardiovascular risk via inflammasome-primed macrophages, and predicts therapy-related MDS/AML after PARP inhibitors, platinum, and radioligand therapy. For plasma testing, blood-cell clones can contribute variants that require origin assessment using matched blood-cell data, tumour evidence and the stated assay limits; some assignments remain ambiguous. Interventions are preventive (avoid unnecessary genotoxic exposure, monitor) with IL-1β/IL-6 blockade under study.

links.label: Jaiswal et al., Age-related clonal hematopoiesis associated with adverse outcomes (NEJM 2014)
Bolton et al., Cancer therapy shapes the fitness landscape of clonal hematopoiesis (Nature Genetics 2020)
High-intensity sequencing reveals the sources of plasma circulating cell-free DNA variants
Therapy-Related Clonal Hematopoiesis in Patients with Non-hematologic Cancers Is Common and Associated with Adverse Clinical Outcomes
Steensma2015
Khoury et al.: WHO myeloid and histiocytic/dendritic classification (2022)
Shah et al., 2012: clonal and mutational evolution in primary triple-negative breast cancer

notes: Leading programmes: Ebert (Dana-Farber/Broad) and Jaiswal (Stanford) who defined CHIP; Levine and Bolton (MSK) on therapy-related clonal haematopoiesis.

Clonal haematopoiesis (CH) is the broader phenomenon of blood-cell clones carrying acquired changes. In the 2022 WHO myeloid classification, CHIP requires a somatic mutation in a myeloid-malignancy-associated gene at a variant allele fraction of at least 2%, or at least 4% for X-linked gene mutations in males, without a diagnosed haematological disorder or unexplained cytopenia (Khoury 2022). Persistent unexplained cytopenia changes the classification question. These are criteria for a named category, not a rule that every smaller blood-cell clone is absent, tumour-derived or a sequencing error.

Which genes: in blood-cell exomes from 17,182 people most clonal variants fell in DNMT3A, TET2 and ASXL1, were rare before age 40, and were seen in 9.5% of people aged 70 to 79 (Jaiswal 2014). ASXL1 mutations were enriched in current or former smokers, and radiation, platinum and topoisomerase II inhibitors selected for DNA-damage-response genes (TP53, PPM1D, CHEK2), with sequential samples showing those clones outgrowing others after exposure (Bolton 2020). In 8,810 people with non-haematological cancers, PPM1D and TP53 mutations were associated with prior chemotherapy, and clonal haematopoiesis was found in 25% (Coombs 2017).

Source attribution in plasma, interpretation rule: TP53 is a tumour gene and also a therapy-selected blood-cell gene, so a TP53 variant in plasma after chemotherapy can come from either compartment. Matched white-blood-cell DNA and the tumour's variant list, where available, help assess its origin; some variants remain ambiguous. In Razavi's paired sequencing 53.2% of cfDNA mutations in 124 people with metastatic cancer and 81.6% in 47 controls without cancer had features of clonal haematopoiesis, and variants that could not be separated from white-blood-cell DNA kept an explicit ambiguous category, so subtracting every blood match is not a complete attribution method.

Fictional example: a plasma assay detects a variant that sensitive matched blood-cell sequencing finds at 0.8% VAF. The blood result supports a blood-cell contribution even below the 2% cut-off, but it does not make the variant CHIP or exclude a tumour contribution, because tumour evidence, shared variants and each method's limits still apply. Matched sequencing has its own gene coverage, depth and detection rules, so a clone below its sensitivity can stay unseen, and a clone finding is not a leukaemia diagnosis or a solid-tumour treatment instruction.

Reading the figures: a variant allele fraction counts variant alleles among the alleles evaluated and is not automatically the percentage of cells. Acquired (somatic) means not inherited and does not mean malignant. There is no age at which a plasma variant can simply be dismissed. Sequential samples show clones with DNA-damage-response mutations outgrowing others after radiation, platinum or topoisomerase II inhibitor exposure (Bolton 2020), which is selection of clones that can already be present and does not mean every new detection was caused by treatment.

For an origin comparison, keep plasma, extracted blood-cell DNA and any separately sampled tumour clearly identified, with collection dates relative to treatment. The report needs the variants, coverage, allele fractions, detection limits, identity and contamination checks, and any unresolved source assignment. A clone result alone does not locate a solid-tumour lesion, predict whether that particular clone will progress, or choose a solid-tumour drug. A later blood-cell comparator can help, but it is not a time-matched measurement of the earlier sample. A clone-classification rule or origin filter does not itself establish regulatory approval or clinical validation of the sequencing method.

A gene name does not settle a plasma variant's source. Shah and colleagues found TP53 to be the most frequently mutated gene in their 2012 primary triple-negative breast-cancer cohort; Bolton's 2020 study found that radiation, platinum and topoisomerase II inhibitor exposure selected blood-cell clones with TP53 and other DNA-damage-response mutations. Those are different populations and compartments. A tumour reference and a matched blood-cell comparison help answer different questions, each within its own coverage and sensitivity. A newly confirmed tumour alteration can also reflect evolution rather than a blood-cell clone or technical noise.

Prostate cancer: this is where clonal haematopoiesis does concrete harm. In 69 men with advanced prostate cancer, clonal haematopoiesis variants at 2% or more were present in plasma from 13, 19%, and 7, 10%, had one in a gene used to decide PARP inhibitor candidacy, most often ATM, accounting for almost half of all somatic DNA repair variants detected. A paired whole-blood control distinguishes them (Jensen 2021).
records.analogy: Weeds in the blood's seed bank. Harmless individually, they spread with age and after chemical sprays, some turn into leukaemia, and their DNA litters the blood, so a test for tumour DNA can mistake weeds for cancer.
interventions: Paired white-blood-cell sequencing in liquid biopsy pipelines
Monitoring after PARP inhibitors and radioligand therapy
IL-1β/IL-6 blockade trials for CHIP-associated cardiovascular risk

records.name: Hot vs cold tumours
records.tldr: Hot, excluded and desert describe where specified immune cells were found in sampled tissue. Their location alone does not establish tumour recognition, effective killing or benefit from a particular drug.
records.summary:
An inflamed or hot pattern has specified immune cells within sampled tumour regions. In an excluded pattern, cells concentrate in surrounding stroma or at a boundary with less entry into malignant nests. A desert has few relevant cells in the examined regions. Cold is used for desert alone or for both desert and excluded patterns, so state the definition. A macrophage-rich sample is not automatically T-cell inflamed.

These are observations about identity and location. Some infiltrating T cells recognize viral or other non-cancer antigens; others restrain responses. Region, specimen, disease site and sampling time matter, and treatment can change the pattern. Neither a small biopsy nor a pattern label describes every site in a person or selects an immunotherapy. Exclusion suggests questions about recruitment, vessels, matrix and local cells, rather than proving one causal wall.

notes: In a fictional comparison, inflamed and excluded fields each contain eight specified T-cell symbols, relocated from mainly within malignant regions to surrounding stroma; a desert field has two. Equal counts can conceal different locations. Region outlines do not prove a physical barrier, these counts do not describe all mononuclear cells used in stromal TIL scoring, and they cannot be converted to an sTIL area percentage. The example depicts neither lymph-node follicles nor tertiary lymphoid organization and supplies no clinical cutoff or response rate.

Routine pathology can score a defined infiltrate, multiplex imaging adds selected cell identities and coordinates, and mixed-tissue gene expression describes programmes without directly retaining each cell’s location. Report the preparation, section, sampled regions, staining and cell-assignment rules, regional variation, output and denominator. Descriptive labels, cells per area and method-defined stromal scores are different outputs. Sectioning and staining use finite tissue. Damage, staining error, incorrect boundaries and an unrepresentative region can limit the result. A research classifier needs separate validation for a clinical selection use.

In Loi’s pooled analysis of 2,148 early TNBC patients given anthracycline-based adjuvant chemotherapy with or without taxanes, each 10 percentage-point increase in stromal TILs was associated with iDFS HR 0.87 and OS HR 0.84. This is prognosis in that population, not proof of additional checkpoint-drug benefit by hot/cold category. Taube’s tissue study also supports coexistence of lymphocyte infiltration and induced inhibitory PD-L1; hot does not mean every later immune step succeeds.

Pancreatic examples have specific settings. Feig’s pancreatic mouse model connected FAP-positive fibroblast CXCL12 with T-cell exclusion; Yamamoto’s work identified autophagy-dependent class-I degradation and tested immune rescue in mice. These are not measurements of every human pancreatic tumour. Royal’s 27-person ipilimumab study reported no RECIST responses but one delayed regression after initial progression. O’Reilly’s 65-person metastatic study reported objective response rates of 3.1% with durvalumab plus tremelimumab and 0% with durvalumab alone, without meeting its expansion threshold. These historical studies do not establish a complete treatment-selection rule or prove that one molecular subgroup is the only possible responder population.

records.name: Companion diagnostic
records.tldr: A companion diagnostic provides information required for a corresponding treatment to be used safely and effectively within its specified context. The result is one part of a treatment decision.
records.summary: The category concerns a device and a corresponding treatment use. FDA describes roles involving likely benefit, serious-adverse-effect risk or specified treatment monitoring. Check both the treatment and diagnostic labeling, including specimen, disease, biomarker and decision rule. A molecular report listing a drug is not by itself a companion-diagnostic authorization. Similar gene names do not establish assay interchangeability, and a positive result does not promise a response.

Whether to repeat a measurement or use another specimen depends on the actual test and laboratory criteria.

records.name: Controlled perturbation experiment
records.tldr: Controlled perturbations deliberately change specified factors and compare responses with suitable controls. A model response alone does not prove its mechanism or patient benefit.
records.summary: A controlled perturbation deliberately changes a defined factor and measures the response against appropriate comparison conditions. Vehicle, positive, negative and mechanism controls answer different questions. A reproducible response can support an experimental claim without establishing its proposed mechanism or patient benefit. Baseline growth, timing, dose and the actual unit assigned to treatment matter.

links.label: Hafner et al.: growth rate inhibition metrics correct for confounders in measuring drug sensitivity (Nature Methods 2016)
Measuring cancer drug sensitivity and resistance in cultured cells (Current Protocols in Chemical Biology 2017)

notes: A vehicle control contains the carrier without the active treatment; an untreated condition asks a different question if the carrier has effects. A positive control checks that the assay can detect a known relevant response, while a negative or non-targeting control estimates background under its design. Another independent way to disrupt the same function can support a mechanism, and a rescue restores a function to test whether that reverses the response here. Off-target effects, incomplete restoration and model context limit interpretation. These are questions for matched model, timing and readout; no one control proves specificity or patient benefit, and agreement between similar readouts is not automatically independent mechanistic confirmation.

Keep what changed, the comparator, concentration or dose range, timing, assignment, readout and units, sample identities, replicate structure and variability. Repeated wells address variation under their preparation and allocation; independently obtained biological samples address another source of variation. Many wells from one tumour do not become independent patients, and repetition or a small p-value does not repair a missing comparison. A two-drug experiment needs vehicle, both single drugs and the combination. A larger combination effect than either single drug is not automatically synergy; that claim needs a stated reference model.

Fictional direct counts: vehicle-treated cells increase from 100 to 200 while drug-treated cells remain at 100. The endpoint drug count is half the vehicle count without measured net decline from the starting count, so calling it 50 per cent killing overstates the observation. Slower growth, death and a molecular change require their own readouts; direct death or recovery measurements could address further questions. Hafner and colleagues showed that conventional IC50 and maximal-effect measures depend on cell divisions during an assay and developed growth-rate metrics to address that dependence. A real experimental response does not by itself establish the responsible target or clinical benefit.

A fictional two-drug table normalises remaining viability to vehicle at 100 per cent: A leaves 70, B leaves 80, and combination examples leave 56 or 30. Highest single agent uses the better single-drug effect, a 70 per cent remaining-viability reference here. Bliss independence predicts 0.70 times 0.80 = 0.56, or 56 per cent. Both combinations exceed the HSA effect; 56 matches Bliss while 30 exceeds it at that dose pair. A further combination leaving 65 exceeds HSA but not Bliss. Loewe additivity instead needs equivalent-dose information from suitable individual dose-response curves; this one-point table cannot establish it. Report the model, dose-pair pattern, uncertainty and schedule. Interaction relative to a reference does not identify a biological mechanism, tolerable human exposure or a treatment choice.

A rescue restores a proposed missing function or supply and tests whether a defined effect reverses. Adding a cake mix back after its removal implicates the mixture without identifying flour, sugar or another ingredient; likewise, broad mevalonate add-back does not isolate cholesterol. More specific branch perturbations and appropriate add-backs can narrow the explanation. Partial rescue can reflect incomplete delivery or restoration as well as additional contributors, so it does not prove a second cause. Place the add-back relative to the blocked step: supplying GGPP after an upstream synthesis block is different from inhibiting the transferase that uses GGPP, which the added substrate cannot simply be assumed to bypass. Include restoration-only and matched controls, verify the restored process and distinguish growth, morphology and death. A genetic perturbation also has its own specificity limits.

Attribute each readout to the relevant cells. An ATP-based signal can change through cell number or per-cell metabolism, and slower single-cell mass accumulation does not by itself show death. Direct death measurements and regrowth after washout ask further questions; regrowth concerns surviving cells, not revival of cells already dead. A mixed culture can change composition, and a nonmalignant-cell label alone does not establish a validated healthy-tissue control. Ladan's breast-slice chemotherapy assay was compared with response during preoperative treatment in a defined setting. That assay-specific validation does not validate every postoperative combination, human exposure or clinical decision. An inadequate viable preparation should remain uninterpretable rather than be called resistant.

records.name: Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA)
records.tldr: Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) consists of fragments of DNA shed by tumour cells into the blood, detectable with sensitive sequencing.
records.summary: Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) is made up of DNA fragments shed by tumour cells into the bloodstream, where they form only a small fraction of all cell-free DNA and are detected with sensitive sequencing. Its uses span genotyping for companion diagnostics, tracking resistance mutations such as EGFR T790M and ESR1, molecular residual disease, early detection and response monitoring. Shedding varies with tumour type and burden, and clonal haematopoiesis can confound results. The term underpins the Liquid biopsy (ctDNA), MRD / molecular residual disease testing and Multi-cancer early detection (MCED) technologies, and it appears in the SERENA-6, CIRCULATE-Japan and IMvigor011 trials and in ideas on molecular-progression switching beyond ESR1 and HPV ctDNA to guide cervical cancer therapy.

links.label: Wikipedia
Detection of Circulating Tumor DNA in Early- and Late-Stage Human Malignancies
High-intensity sequencing reveals the sources of plasma circulating cell-free DNA variants

notes: Detection depends on stage and tumour type: with digital PCR-based methods in 640 patients, ctDNA was found in more than 75% of people with advanced pancreatic, ovarian, colorectal, bladder, gastro-oesophageal, breast, melanoma, hepatocellular and head and neck cancers, and in fewer than 50% of primary brain, renal, prostate or thyroid cancers. In localised disease it was found in 73% of colorectal, 57% of gastro-oesophageal, 48% of pancreatic and 50% of breast adenocarcinomas, and it was often present in people with no detectable circulating tumour cells (Bettegowda 2014). The assay, specimen and population are part of each figure.

ctDNA is a subset of cell-free DNA, and not every plasma variant is tumour-derived: in paired plasma and white-blood-cell sequencing, 53.2% of cfDNA mutations in 124 people with metastatic cancer and 81.6% in 47 people without cancer had features of clonal haematopoiesis (Razavi 2019). A ctDNA result is also a quantity with a unit (molecules per millilitre, a fraction, or a call), and the same number means different things under each.

Lung cancer: plasma genotyping at diagnosis is non-inferior to tissue for finding a guideline biomarker (27.3% against 21.3% in 282 patients), has 100% positive predictive value for the alterations with approved drugs, returns in 9 days against 15, and raises detection by 48% when added to tissue (Leighl 2019). Clinical sensitivity against tissue is 80%, so a negative plasma result rules nothing out and the guideline permits plasma to rule in only (Lindeman 2018). Serial plasma after starting treatment also separates the patients whose resistant clone was already present, within three weeks (Oxnard 2018).

records.name: ctDNA and imaging discordance
records.tldr: A blood DNA result and an imaging result can seem to disagree because they sample different material, regions, times and signals. A mismatch is a question to resolve, not a verdict on either test.
records.summary:
A circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) assay looks for tumour-associated features in a finite sample of cell-free DNA. How much tumour DNA reaches the sampled blood varies between lesions, and recovery, background DNA, the features tracked and the assay's detection limit all shape the call. Imaging measures a defined region through a physical signal. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the breast can report contrast enhancement or the volume of enhancing tissue, which is not a direct count of viable cancer cells. The two tests can therefore differ without either being wrong, and neither automatically replaces the other.

They can also share information. In Magbanua and colleagues' pilot of 84 women having neoadjuvant chemotherapy for early breast cancer, ctDNA concentration was correlated with MRI functional tumour volume at all four time points, with Spearman correlations of 0.42 to 0.49, and patients with detectable ctDNA had a higher median volume. Agreement was partial, and adding ctDNA early in treatment to volume-based prediction of pathological complete response gave only a numerical gain that was not statistically significant. ctDNA positivity after treatment added significantly to volume for predicting distant recurrence and death. A mismatch calls for checking dates, assay limits, the imaged region and the exact finding. It does not by itself show a false test or hidden metastatic disease.

notes: Method card, what is compared: a sampled molecular signal in plasma and a regional physical signal from a named imaging protocol. Their units, dates and thresholds stay separate, and the comparison is only as good as the date alignment of the two acquisitions.

Table, blood side: input is a blood draw and the plasma and recovered DNA analysed, and testing consumes an aliquot. Output is a qualifying call plus a defined concentration or fraction, read with the assay's detection and quantitation rules. Failure modes are low shedding, finite input, poor recovery and background or blood-cell variants.

Table, imaging side: input is the imaged region and a protocol, and contrast or tracer use depends on the modality. Output is size, volume, uptake or a qualitative finding read against protocol-specific response criteria. Failure modes are artefacts, non-tumour contributions to the signal and technique that differs between visits.

Table, what each cannot tell: blood alone cannot locate a lesion or give a cell count. Imaging alone cannot count viable tumour cells, and enhancement can have more than one tissue cause. Neither agreement nor disagreement shows that a treatment change would help, which is a clinical-utility question.

Evidence read: Magbanua's pilot (84 patients, MTM/mL against MRI functional tumour volume) found correlation at T0 to T3 with rho 0.49, 0.42, 0.42 and 0.43, and its authors call the findings preliminary in a limited cohort needing larger validation. It supports partial agreement and does not set a rule for redirecting treatment.

Interpretation rule, from finite sampling: a plasma aliquot can hold no tumour molecule when the true share is small, so no qualifying ctDNA signal alongside an abnormal MRI region does not show the region is only scar. The converse holds too: a clear image does not exclude tumour DNA in blood. Each result answers only its own question.

Source attribution comes first: a positive plasma variant may come from a blood-cell clone rather than a tumour. In Razavi's paired sequencing, 53.2% of cell-free DNA mutations in 124 people with metastatic cancer and 81.6% in 47 people without cancer had features of clonal haematopoiesis, so a discordant positive needs origin checks before it is read as occult disease.

Half-life, scoped: Diehl and colleagues estimated a ctDNA half-life after surgery of 114 minutes by evaluating one subject whose plasma was sampled at several early times after complete resection in a study of 162 plasma samples from 18 subjects with colorectal cancer (Diehl 2008). That is a single-subject estimate of post-resection clearance in colorectal cancer, not a universal cfDNA half-life, a breast-cancer figure or a blood-draw schedule. DNA release and clearance can change sooner than visible tissue structure, which is a reason to align the dates of the blood and imaging acquisitions.

Use the blood collection date and imaging acquisition date to compare biology, then keep the reporting dates as a separate measure of when the information became available. Imaging does not remove a tissue aliquot for molecular analysis; contrast or tracer use belongs to the specific protocol. Agreement can reflect shared dependence on disease burden and is not two independent proofs of the same mechanism. Combining measurements into a decision rule needs validation of the combination and its intended outcome.

In a fictional early-breast-cancer example, a negative plasma result is not an examination of the breast tumour bed or regional nodes. It cannot by itself establish pathological complete response or validate skipping surgery. Using a result to remove a treatment needs evidence for that decision strategy and its clinical outcomes, beyond showing that an assay can detect a signal. This is an interpretation limit, not a claim that no omission study exists.

The two-window comparison is about scope. A finite plasma aliquot contains extracellular DNA, of which tumour-derived fragments may be one part; breast MRI observes regional, sequence-dependent features rather than individual cancer cells. Contrast enhancement reflects vascular and contrast-delivery behaviour as well as the acquisition protocol; it is not a one-to-one viable-cell count. In the 84-person I-SPY2 MRI pilot, functional tumour volume summed voxels meeting 70% enhancement about two and a half minutes after contrast, inside a manually drawn box around the lesion. A camera-and-stream analogy illustrates those two sampled views without promising that every tumour sheds DNA. Keep the imaging method visible: mammography uses X-rays, ultrasound uses sound, and PET/CT combines tracer-distribution images with anatomical CT images. A formal response category needs its framework, comparison timepoint and findings outside a selected lesion measurement. None of these measurements is an interchangeable all-body tumour-cell number.

Four patterns illustrate the reading boundary. A smaller lesion and lower detected blood signal mean that both recorded measures fell in their own units, not that pCR or eradication of distant disease is proved. A residual scan finding with undetected blood leaves viability, treatment effects and other causes unresolved. Detected blood with no suspicious finding in the scanned region does not establish the signal's location, full extent or best intervention. If neither shows qualifying evidence, neither has proved zero microscopic disease or justified omitting indicated treatment. These are interpretation examples, not an action algorithm; disagreement alone does not establish pseudoprogression.

In a fictional course, a breast lesion becomes less enhancing, blood changes from detected to not detected, and surgery later finds residual invasive cancer. There is no contradiction: imaging features, a finite molecular sample and removed tissue answer different questions. Only the specified tissue assessment establishes the residual disease in this example. A smaller scan finding and undetected blood can therefore be favourable observations without confirming pCR. Conversely, a later positive blood result with clear regional breast imaging calls for review of sample qualification, origin, dates and clinical context; it is not itself a diagnosis of distant metastasis.

Magbanua and colleagues' 2025 analysis evaluated 723 high-risk I-SPY2 patients across hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative, triple-negative and HER2-positive subtypes. Combining ctDNA with residual cancer burden refined prognostic groups, but analyses within those groups used smaller subsets, some too small for multivariable adjustment. The authors also found retained patient-specific assay variants in sampled resistant tumours from patients whose post-treatment plasma was negative. These results support studying risk information and shedding; they do not turn negative presurgical blood into tissue pCR or demonstrate that a blood-guided omission strategy improves outcomes.

records.name: ctDNA units, fractions and concentrations
records.tldr: A ctDNA result is a number with a unit. Molecules per millilitre, parts per million and allele fraction answer different questions, so a printed number means nothing until its unit and denominator are known.
records.summary:
Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) can be reported as a concentration, as a fraction, or as a yes or no call, and the three are not interchangeable. A concentration counts tumour-attributed molecules in a stated volume of plasma. One example is mean tumour molecules per millilitre (MTM/mL), which the I-SPY 2 breast-cancer study of Magbanua and colleagues used for ctDNA across tracked variants. A fraction divides tumour-attributed molecules by a stated total, such as all evaluated alleles at one position (variant allele fraction, VAF) or all evaluated DNA (an estimated tumour fraction). Parts per million (PPM) is a fraction multiplied by one million, so the number is only as meaningful as the fraction it scales: 0.01% is 100 PPM, and 0.00024% is 2.4 PPM, the lowest allele fraction Santonja and colleagues reported for ctDNA detection in breast cancer.

Concentration and fraction can move apart. If two equal one-millilitre aliquots each hold the same number of tumour molecules but one holds more background cell-free DNA, the concentration is unchanged and the fraction falls. A detection call and a reliable amount are also different claims, because the detection limit and the quantitation range are validated separately. Nothing here gives a conversion between assays: MTM/mL cannot be turned into PPM from the printed result, and a VAF of 100 PPM at one variant is not a tumour fraction of 100 PPM.

Santonja et al., EMBO Mol Med 2023: tumour-informed and tumour-naive ctDNA assays compared, allele fractions to 2.4 parts per million
FDA, Use of Circulating Tumor DNA for Curative-Intent Solid Tumor Drug Development, November 2024

notes: Method card, what it measures: the quantity an assay states, either a count of tumour-attributed molecules per volume of plasma (a concentration), a share of a named total (a fraction), or a call. How: sequencing or PCR on one finite plasma aliquot, then a calculation the laboratory defines. Keep the unit, the denominator and the assay version attached to every value.

Table, MTM/mL: mean tumour molecules per millilitre of plasma under the assay's own calculation across its tracked features. Boundary: a concentration estimated from tracked features, not the number of cancer cells per millilitre and not a share of anything.

Table, PPM: parts per million, a fraction multiplied by one million, so 1 PPM is 0.0001% and 100 PPM is 0.01%. Boundary: name the fraction being scaled, because 100 PPM of variant alleles, of evaluated DNA and of tumour-attributed molecules are three different claims.

Table, variant allele fraction: the share of evaluated alleles at one position that carry a stated variant. Boundary: it depends on copy number, on which clones carry the variant and on the measurement, and a variant present in a blood-cell clone counts the same way as one from a tumour.

Table, tumour fraction: an estimated share of evaluated DNA attributable to tumour. Boundary: it is a model output that rests on the method and its calibration, and it is not automatically any single variant's VAF.

Fictional arithmetic, concentration against fraction: two equal 1 mL aliquots each hold 4 tumour-attributed molecules. Aliquot A also holds 16 background molecules, so 4 of 20 is 20% and the concentration is 4 molecules per mL. Aliquot B holds 36 background molecules, so 4 of 40 is 10% and the concentration is still 4 per mL. More background lowered the fraction and left the concentration alone. These toy shares are not a VAF, an estimated tumour fraction or MTM/mL.

Fictional arithmetic, rescaling: a VAF of 0.01% at Variant R equals 100 PPM of variant-supporting alleles. That does not make a tumour fraction of 100 PPM, and a second report of 0.2 MTM/mL is a concentration, so 100 and 0.2 cannot be compared or converted without the methods and calibration of both assays.

Method limit, detection against quantitation: a qualifying detection call and a reliable numerical amount have separate validation criteria. A detected value below the validated quantitative range does not support an exact fold change, and extra decimal places do not create precision.

Method limit, finite input: the plasma volume drawn is not the volume or the number of molecules recovered and evaluated. Low molecular counts, changes in background DNA, poor recovery or incompatible calibration all limit comparison across assays, and a printed zero is not a count of zero cancer cells anywhere in the body.

Evidence read: in Magbanua's 84-patient pilot of neoadjuvant treatment, ctDNA in MTM/mL was correlated with MRI functional tumour volume at every time point (Spearman rho 0.42 to 0.49). Santonja's comparison reported allele fractions down to 2.4 PPM for hybrid-capture sequencing of 1,347 to 7,491 tumour-identified mutations and 4.7 PPM for multiplex PCR of 21 to 47 structural variants. Each figure belongs to its assay and cohort.

A trend also needs the collection time, treatment context, assay version and quantitative range. In its November 2024 drug-development guidance, FDA asks for precision, accuracy and detection-limit evaluation across relevant inputs and cut-offs, using representative clinical specimens and appropriately comparable reference material. A printed number below another assay's nominal detection limit does not establish that the other assay would miss that sample: the measured quantity, specimen, input, recovery and calling rules may differ. A reference-material result is not automatically a clinical sensitivity estimate.

Consider a fictional assay estimating tumour fraction at 6 parts per million (PPM) and then 2 PPM. Both samples are called detected, but the second is below the assay's reliable quantitation range. The printed estimates fall by two-thirds; they do not establish that the cancer volume fell by two-thirds. Retain the qualifying calls and uncertainty, because shedding and background DNA can change the signal. A second method reporting molecules per millilitre cannot simply be placed on this fraction scale. Even a matching unit label does not establish matching calibration. Keeping serial methods and input comparable helps interpretation without removing biological variation.

The blank, detection and quantitation limits answer different questions. The blank limit is the highest apparent analyte concentration expected from replicate samples with no analyte; the detection limit is the lowest concentration reliably distinguished from that background; the quantitation limit is the lowest concentration meeting predefined bias and imprecision goals (Armbruster and Pry, 2008). Quantitation and detection limits may coincide or differ. A qualifying detection below a validated quantitative range supports presence more strongly than an exact fold change. For a read-based variant allele fraction, the denominator is informative reads covering that locus, not cancer cells or plasma volume; keep a molecule-based method's own definition instead.

records.name: DESTINY-Breast04
records.tldr: DESTINY-Breast04 compared trastuzumab deruxtecan with chemotherapy in previously treated HER2-low metastatic breast cancer. Its results concern the enrolled score categories and clinical setting.
records.summary:
DESTINY-Breast04 (NCT03734029) randomised 557 patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer after one or two prior lines of chemotherapy: 494 were hormone receptor-positive and 63 hormone receptor-negative at randomisation. HER2-low meant IHC 1+ or IHC 2+/ISH-negative. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival in the hormone receptor-positive cohort; key secondary endpoints included overall-population progression-free survival and overall survival. The 2022 report showed longer progression-free and overall survival with trastuzumab deruxtecan.

The study did not randomize IHC 0 tumours and does not establish a universal HER2-expression floor, biological category or eligibility for everyone with HER2-negative disease. Exploratory hormone receptor-negative analyses use their specified efficacy populations, distinct from the randomised stratification count. The later Nature Medicine report and current drug label are separate dated sources, not interchangeable versions of the original result.

records.name: DNA
records.tldr: DNA stores sequence information. Its packaging, copying and use as a template for RNA are different processes.
records.summary: DNA contains nucleotide chains with a sugar–phosphate backbone and the bases A, T, C and G. Complementary A–T and C–G pairing joins antiparallel strands. Nuclear chromosomes contain DNA associated with proteins as chromatin; nucleosomes organize DNA around histones. Mitochondria carry a separate genome. A gene is a functional region within DNA, rather than an entire chromosome. Replication copies DNA, while transcription produces RNA from a selected template. Packaging and gene presence do not establish active transcription or a functional protein.
