notes: A composite score compresses selected features of a tumour's chromosome history. Like a summary of past events, it leaves details out; like numbers on differently calibrated scales, the same numerical value need not have the same meaning in two laboratories. The composite count is not a percentage of repair-deficient cells. Copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity can replace two parental versions with copies of one version without reducing the total copy number, so loss of heterozygosity is not always loss of a physical chromosome copy.

Telli 2016 selected the boundary of 42 using an independent training set of 497 breast and 561 ovarian cancers, including 78 breast and 190 ovarian cancers classified as lacking a functional BRCA1 or BRCA2 copy. That classification used a deleterious variant with loss of the other copy, two deleterious changes in one gene, or BRCA1 promoter methylation with loss of the other copy. The boundary was the fifth percentile among these BRCA-deficient cancers, aiming to capture about 95 per cent, rather than an optimised divider of drug responders. Some deficient cancers therefore fall below it. The study's abstract and discussion use at least 42, whereas its Methods prints greater than 42; a result at the boundary needs the actual validated assay rule, not an improvised inequality.

Telli tested the unweighted LOH plus TAI plus LST score in three platinum-containing neoadjuvant triple-negative breast cancer trials, using a high score or a deleterious or suspected-deleterious tumour BRCA1/2 alteration. A variant of uncertain significance did not count as a mutated BRCA result. The odds ratios for minimal residual disease, residual cancer burden class 0 or I, were 4.96 in PrECOG's platinum, gemcitabine and iniparib cohort and 10.18 in the pooled two cisplatin cohorts. These associations are not three randomised demonstrations of extra platinum benefit. PRIMA later defined HRD positivity by a tumour BRCA mutation or a MyChoice genomic instability score of at least 42. That trial definition and current prescribing conditions are separate facts.

ARIEL2 Part 1 used a prespecified 14 per cent genomic-LOH cutoff in relapsed, platinum-sensitive high-grade ovarian cancer. Of 206 enrolled patients, 204 received rucaparib and 192 could be classified: 40 BRCA-mutated, 82 BRCA-wild-type/LOH-high and 70 BRCA-wild-type/LOH-low. Twelve BRCA-wild-type tumours lacked enough neoplastic nuclei for the LOH classification. This percentage of genome is a different quantity from the composite sum, and a single-arm rucaparib study cannot by itself separate prognostic association from differential treatment benefit. HRDetect is different again: its weighted sequence-signature logistic model outputs a probability of BRCA-deficient genomic history. Its 2017 sensitivity and AUC describe that classification task, not an individual's chance of benefiting from a medicine.

In the GeparSixto analysis, HRD was measurable in 193 of 315 triple-negative breast cancers. Pathological complete response rose from 33.9 to 63.5 per cent with added carboplatin in the HR-deficient group and from 20.0 to 29.6 per cent in the other group. The treatment-by-HRD interaction had P = 0.327. This does not establish that the treatment effects differ by HRD status, nor does a non-significant interaction prove they are identical. In TNT, 376 people with advanced triple-negative disease or a germline BRCA-associated breast cancer received carboplatin or docetaxel. Germline-BRCA carriers had response rates of 68 versus 33 per cent, with interaction P = 0.01; a high Myriad HRD score did not select extra carboplatin benefit. Association with response and evidence for choosing between treatments are different questions.

PAOLA-1 randomised 806 people with advanced ovarian cancer responding to first-line platinum-taxane chemotherapy plus bevacizumab. Both maintenance groups received bevacizumab; the added treatment was olaparib or placebo. The 2019 HRD-positive progression-free-survival hazard ratio was 0.33, with a 95 per cent interval of 0.25 to 0.45. The olaparib label's planned exploratory HRD-negative analysis gives 1.00, with an interval of 0.75 to 1.34. That interval is compatible with a range of effects and does not prove exactly zero benefit. It also cannot be transferred to an unrelated assay, breast cancer, a different drug or olaparib without bevacizumab.

PRIMA's 2019 analysis randomised 733 people after response to first-line platinum for advanced ovarian cancer. Among 373 with HR-deficient tumours, median progression-free survival was 21.9 versus 10.4 months with niraparib versus placebo, hazard ratio 0.43 with a 95 per cent interval of 0.31 to 0.59. In the overall population it was 13.8 versus 8.2 months, hazard ratio 0.62 with an interval of 0.50 to 0.76. These are historical progression-free-survival results, not an updated overall-survival estimate. The U.S. niraparib label effective July 2026 restricts first-line maintenance to HRD-positive advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer in complete or partial response to platinum, selected with an authorised companion test.

The U.S. olaparib label effective July 2025 permits olaparib plus bevacizumab maintenance for adults with HRD-positive advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer in complete or partial response to first-line platinum; the specified HRD definition includes a deleterious or suspected-deleterious BRCA alteration and/or genomic instability, with an approved companion test. Its early-breast indication instead requires a deleterious or suspected-deleterious germline BRCA alteration, HER2-negative high-risk disease and prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy, with the approved test. A tumour-only BRCA finding or an arbitrary high scar number does not substitute for these conditions.

The specimen and analysis are part of the result. Telli used tumour DNA, a genome-wide SNP panel, allele-imbalance profiles and prespecified counting rules; if the score failed and BRCA testing was negative or failed, HRD status was undetermined. A failed result is not a low score. Reports should identify the assay version, usable tumour content, DNA input/quality, copy-number and allele-balance method, segmentation, and purity/ploidy assumptions. HRDetect was explored in a small biopsy series and one formalin-fixed specimen with substantial sequencing artefact; those demonstrations do not certify every degraded specimen. RAD51 foci ask a different, conditional question about present repair. A BRCA reversion or 53BP1 loss is not itself a measured new scar score or proof of restored function.

In a fictional report, laboratory X gives a score of 48 and a paper uses laboratory Y's cutoff of 42 in early triple-negative breast cancer. The numerical comparison 48 > 42 does not establish HRD positivity on X's assay: its scale, quality requirements and validated boundary are needed. Even on the correct scale, association with response to one regimen does not establish extra carboplatin benefit over a comparator. GeparSixto's interaction analysis and TNT's high-score result illustrate that distinction; neither permits a blanket claim that a high-score tumour never benefits from carboplatin.
records.principle: Assay-specific counts or weighted sequence signatures describe selected genomic patterns. Their scales, validated boundaries and clinical uses differ; they do not directly measure present repair or drug sensitivity.
strengths: Can identify genomic patterns beyond a BRCA sequence finding
Selected ovarian maintenance indications use validated companion tests
Permits explicit comparison of assay methods and their validation populations
limitations: Historical scars can coexist with restored repair
Assay scales and validated cutoffs differ
Specimen quality and tumour content can prevent an interpretable result

records.name: Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
records.tldr: Staining a tissue slice with antibodies so a protein shows up in colour under the microscope.
records.summary: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) uses antibody binding and signal development to show a selected protein in a prepared tissue section. Interpretation retains which cells and compartments stain, the intensity and distribution, and the named marker-specific method. A percentage, intensity category or composite score can describe different aspects of the result. Fixation, retrieval, controls, sampling and observer variation affect interpretation. Automated quantification also needs validation for its marker, specimens and intended use. A research stain or generic score does not replace a validated clinical selection assay.

links.label: Wikipedia
Measurement method and interpretation source
RCPath breast dataset, Table 8, Allred and H-score conventions
Targeted peptide measurements in biology and medicine: best practices for mass spectrometry-based assay development using a fit-for-purpose approach (Molecular & cellular proteomics : MCP 2014)

notes: There is no universal IHC scoring scale or positivity threshold. Retain antibody clone, retrieval and detection method, controls, eligible cells, subcellular location, intensity, distribution and intended use. A research stain does not automatically replace a clinical selection assay.

An H-score under the intensity-weighted convention is weak-cell percentage plus twice moderate-cell percentage plus three times strong-cell percentage, on a 0 to 300 scale. Fictional example: 50 unstained, 10 weak, 20 moderate and 20 strong cells out of 100 give 50% positive and H-score 110. Neither is a molecule count.

Bulk receptor abundance and staining mainly on blood vessels can both be correct: one measures a mixture and the other locates signal. Neither establishes target accessibility or treatment benefit. Staining also does not establish protein activity or cancer-cell dependence on that protein.

IHC makes selected proteins visible through antibody binding and signal development in a prepared section. Specificity, retrieval, detection, positive controls, internal controls and background matter. Nuclear and membrane signals answer different questions. Multiplex fluorescence adds markers but still needs validated antibody performance and cell-boundary assignment.

In the conventional Allred scheme, proportion categories are 0 for no positive cells, 1 for less than 1%, 2 for 1% to 10%, 3 for 11% to 33%, 4 for 34% to 66% and 5 for 67% to 100%. Intensity is 0 for absent staining or 1, 2 and 3 for weak, moderate and strong staining. The total is 0 or 2 to 8. In a fictional separate example, 30% positive cells with moderate staining give 3 + 2 = 5. These integer bins are a named convention, not a universal positivity rule.

Equal H-scores can conceal different intensity distributions. A negative clinical category does not establish zero protein molecules. HER2 and hormone-receptor assays have marker-specific reporting rules; current CAP breast reporting retains percentage and intensity even when an optional composite score is given.

A useful IHC result identifies the block, fixation and section, antibody clone, retrieval and detection system, eligible cells and scored compartment. Cutting and staining use finite tissue. Report the percentage, intensity, location and named scoring scale, together with expected-positive tissue, relevant internal controls and background assessment. Poor preservation, nonspecific binding, few eligible cells, heterogeneous staining and observer variation can limit interpretation. Validation must fit the assay and its intended use; a research measurement is not automatically a clinical selection test.

Staining recognises an antibody-defined molecular feature, or epitope, rather than automatically proving a complete functioning protein. In an invented repair-gene example, weaker staining in identified cancer cells than in normal neighbours supports a cell-specific signal difference if the controls are adequate. The antibody may recognise a fragment or more than one protein form, so this does not give the amount of intact useful repair protein. The relevant form and current repair need suitable measurements of their own. One validated method can sometimes answer several questions, but measuring one property does not establish every other one.

records.tldr: Deconvolution estimates which cell populations contributed to a mixed molecular measurement.
records.summary: Deconvolution fits reference cell-type profiles to a mixed profile under a model; similar types, missing populations and state change allow several fits.

notes: Deconvolution fits reference cell-type profiles to a mixed profile under a model; similar types, missing populations and state change allow several fits.
The first quantity can be a share of RNA, not cells; EPIC uses RNA-content assumptions and an uncharacterised component.

Relative estimates may sum to one across represented immune populations leaving total immune content unknown; CIBERSORT absolute mode is an expression-based score, not cells per area; other methods report whole-sample fractions.
CIBERSORTx infers cell-type expression and states; these are computational reconstructions, not single-cell measurements, and do not prove suppressive function, clone or location.
Compare with flow, pathology or spatial data, each with its own bias; validate for tissue, preparation, populations and units.
Fictional teaching exercise: Sample A has 10 T cells among 20 immune cells and sample B 30 among 60 (100 cells each): both 50% of immune cells, but 10% and 30% of the whole sample.

Existing mixture data and reference profiles support computation without further tissue; comparator assays may consume material. Record fit algorithm, reference, denominator, omitted populations and output as relative fraction, whole-sample estimate, abundance score or inferred expression. Runtime and fit filters vary; known mixtures, held-out data and matched measurements test assumptions. Similar signatures, RNA content, state and platform shifts prevent a global fit from certifying every population or clinical use.

records.name: Immune system
records.tldr: The body's defence network of cells and molecules that recognises and destroys infected, foreign and abnormal cells. It kills most would-be cancers before they are ever noticed; the ones that survive have learned to hide from it.
records.summary: Innate immunity uses inherited sensing systems (barriers, soluble defences such as complement, phagocytes such as macrophages and neutrophils, natural killer cells, and sensors of microbial or damage-related features), while adaptive immunity expands T cells and B cells whose diverse antigen receptors are assembled during development and selected by an encounter, with some descendants persisting as memory cells. The two cooperate: dendritic cells, cytokines and lymph nodes connect innate sensing to adaptive responses, and antibodies and T cells in turn guide innate cells.

notes: Fast and memoryless against slow and remembering is a starting tendency and not a rule: mice lacking functional T and B cells were protected against repeat Candida albicans infection in a monocyte-dependent way (Quintin et al., 2012), and natural killer cells carrying the Ly49H receptor expanded about 100-fold in the spleen after mouse cytomegalovirus infection, persisted for months and expanded again after transfer to a new host (Sun et al., 2009).

A list of cell types is a roster and not a functional report: a cell-family name does not show what a cell is doing, a marker shared by several populations is not a complete identity test (single-cell sequencing of human blood found six dendritic-cell and four monocyte subtypes; Villani et al., 2017), and a fraction of immune cells depends on its denominator (percent of recovered immune cells, of T cells and of all tissue cells are different quantities). Blood composition does not substitute for tumour composition, and a count of immune cells in a tumour does not by itself show recognition or killing. CD4 and CD8 are co-receptors and not permanent helper and killer assignments, tumour-associated macrophage names a setting, myeloid-derived suppressor cells need an operational phenotype and a test of suppressive function, and natural killer T cells are a T-cell family distinct from natural killer cells despite the name. In the classical description innate immunity is rapid and without immunologic memory while adaptive immunity is antigen-specific with a capacity for memory, and the two are not mutually exclusive (Marshall et al., 2018). Cytotoxic CD4 T cells have been found in infections, tumours and inflammatory disease, so a CD4 or CD8 label does not fix a helper or killer role (Venkatesh et al., 2023), and a myeloid-derived suppressor cell label rests on myeloid origin plus shown suppressive function (Bronte et al., 2016). CD4 and CD8 are coreceptors for T-cell receptors that recognise MHC, and a review discusses how they help impose MHC specificity during thymic selection (Van Laethem et al., 2012), so a CD4 or CD8 label names a coreceptor and not a job.

Among innate cells, phagocytes (neutrophils and macrophages) engulf and kill microbes, and natural killer cells play a major role in the rejection of tumours and the destruction of virus-infected cells through perforins and granzymes (Marshall et al., 2018). The receptor comparison concerns how recognition equipment is generated: inherited, germline-encoded receptors include Toll-like and natural killer receptors, whereas developing T and B cells assemble diverse antigen receptors by somatic V(D)J recombination (Hayday and Vantourout, 2020; Oettinger et al., 1990; Nemazee, 2017); one review describes the adaptive system as in turn activating innate effector mechanisms in an antigen-specific manner (Medzhitov, 2007).

Most adjuvants are thought to enhance T-cell and B-cell responses by engaging the innate immune system and not the lymphocytes directly (Coffman et al., 2010), so a vaccine can create an inflammatory context, and a response to an unrelated control antigen has to be measured to show that a response to the vaccine antigen is selective; in OnCo's reasoning, a manufactured antibody is also not evidence that the recipient made antibodies. Counts of cells, concentrations in picograms per millilitre and antigen-matched functional assays answer different questions, and a report should say which specimen, which time, which stimulation and which background control was used (OnCo reporting advice).

Tumours are recognised because they display mutated proteins and stress signals, but successful tumours evade destruction by displaying 'don't attack me' checkpoint signals, hiding their antigens, recruiting suppressive cells, and walling themselves off; 'avoiding immune destruction' is one of the hallmarks of cancer. Immunotherapy in its many forms (checkpoint inhibitors, engineered T cells, bispecifics, vaccines) aims to restore or engineer the immune system's ability to see and kill the tumour.

Cell-family roster, T cells: diverse antigen receptors support antigen-specific responses; functions can include help through signals, regulation and target-cell killing. A CD4 or CD8 marker is a coreceptor label, not a permanent helper or killer assignment. Interpretation: the presence of T cells does not establish which antigen they recognise or that killing is occurring (Marshall et al., 2018; Venkatesh et al., 2023).

Cell-family roster, B cells and plasma cells: B cells recognise antigen, can present it to T cells and can produce cytokine signals; plasma cells specialise in antibody secretion (Marshall et al., 2018; de Gruijter et al., 2022). Interpretation: counting either family does not identify what its antibodies bind or whether those antibodies help control a tumour.

Cell-family roster, natural killer cells: activating and inhibitory inputs together influence target-cell damage and cytokine production; these cells can release perforin, granzymes and interferon gamma (Marshall et al., 2018). Interpretation: a count of natural killer cells does not show that every abnormal cell will be attacked. The required signals, cell state and tested target still matter.

Cell-family roster, macrophages: engulfment, antigen presentation and signalling coexist with roles in tissue maintenance and repair. The repair, inflammatory and fibrotic programmes described by Wynn and Vannella (2016) depend on context. Interpretation: a macrophage count or location does not establish a universally beneficial or suppressive function.

Cell-family roster, dendritic cells: they collect and display antigen and provide signals that can shape T-cell priming, connecting innate and adaptive immunity (Marshall et al., 2018). Interpretation: their presence does not establish that the relevant antigen was displayed with the supporting signals needed for a useful response.

Cell-family roster, neutrophils: engulfment and antimicrobial activity are accompanied by inflammatory signalling and tissue effects. Afonso et al. (2012) showed cell-to-cell signal relay by leukotriene B4 in defined neutrophil chemotaxis experiments, including cells from mice with or without the formyl peptide receptor 1. Peiseler and Kubes (2019) review roles in tissue damage, resolution of inflammation and repair, including sterile injury. Interpretation: a neutrophil count alone does not diagnose infection or establish cancer promotion or cancer control.

Recognition-system comparison: innate recognition equipment is inherited; T-cell and B-cell antigen receptors are diversified and assembled during development. Exposure can change innate activation, recruitment and later responsiveness, while an adaptive response can select clones that expand, differentiate and persist as memory. Speed is a separate axis: innate responses are often early but can persist, and adaptive recall can be rapid. Mouse fungal and viral experiments demonstrate particular forms of trained monocyte or memory-like natural killer responses, not a rule that every innate response has conventional T-cell or B-cell memory (Quintin et al., 2012; Sun et al., 2009; Hayday and Vantourout, 2020). Antigen specificity alone does not establish activation or benefit.

Measurement comparison: cell counts describe a sampled population, protein concentration describes an amount per volume, and an antigen-matched functional assay describes an activity under its test conditions. Rodero et al. (2017) measured interferon-alpha protein, interferon-responsive RNA and antiviral activity as different readouts; Sanz et al. (2023) separately measured gamma-delta cell phenotype, receptor repertoire and target-cell killing. The reporting inference is to keep specimen, collection time, cell identity, stimulation, viability and background controls explicit. A concentration in picograms per millilitre is not a cell count or an antigen-specific response.

records.name: Immune-tumour co-culture models
records.tldr: Co-culture places tumour and immune populations together so researchers can measure their interactions with identified cells and appropriate controls.
records.summary: Co-culture studies interactions among defined populations. Dijkstra and colleagues combined autologous blood lymphocytes with tumour organoids from mismatch repair-deficient colorectal cancer and from non-small-cell lung cancer, with enrichment and later killing measurements as separate stages. Neal and colleagues retained native immune components using a specialised air-liquid-interface organoid method. Presence, activation, tumour recognition and killing require different observations; neither model label establishes universal patient prediction.

Neal et al. 2018, Cell: organoid modelling of the tumour immune microenvironment
Functional model interpretation: primary evidence
Permeable-support compartments
Jenkins et al. 2018: organotypic spheroids and retained compartments
Macdonald et al. 2009: human T-cell allorecognition

notes: Controls and compartments. Compare tumour-only, neighbour-only and mixed cultures, with matched vehicle or exposure controls. Direct contact allows contact and exchanged molecules; a selected permeable support can separate cells while allowing exchange, but passage depends on membrane and cells. Previously collected cell-free conditioned medium tests transferred secreted material, not ongoing reciprocal interaction. These comparisons isolate different questions rather than rank culture formats. Source for separated support design: https://www.corning.com/worldwide/en/products/life-sciences/products/permeable-supports/transwell-guidelines.html Autologous populations come from the same person; allogeneic populations come from different people. Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) differences can themselves provoke T-cell recognition in an allogeneic experiment. Macdonald's primary structural study showed HLA- and peptide-dependent human T-cell alloreactivity; it did not validate a tumour-response test. Even autologous cells may lack relevant tumour-reactive cells or change during culture. Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.immuni.2009.09.025

Dijkstra primary study: a two-week enrichment stage preceded a separate three-day organoid-killing assessment. Matched healthy organoids and HLA-blocking comparisons tested specificity; reactions to xenogeneic Geltrex matrix were also investigated. A marker or cytokine signal alone did not substitute for the identified live-cell/death readout. The studied donors and protocol define the scope: the colorectal samples were mismatch repair-deficient, and the defined T-cell response occurred in four of eight patients with MHC class I-positive organoids in the colorectal comparison. No response was observed in the tested MHC class I-deficient lines. These timings are not universal culture windows. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558289/ Jenkins also described organotypic spheroids retaining autologous immune and stromal components. Added blood lymphocytes and retained tumour neighbours are different preparations; measure retention and function over the actual window rather than assign immune capability exclusively to one format. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5809290/

Assay card. Retain source donor/site/time for each viable population, autologous or allogeneic relationship, starting ratio, medium, persistence and readout time. Isolation, expansion and assays consume finite material. Report identified live target counts, a death fraction with denominator, or cytokine concentration with units. Check viability, missing reactive cells, incompatible medium, changing ratios, matrix/allogeneic responses and bulk-signal attribution. Quality thresholds are method-specific; replicates from one donor do not establish population validation.

In a fictional mixed culture, a metabolic signal falls by half, but identified viable tumour-cell counts are unchanged and viable immune-cell counts fall. The bulk decline could come from the immune compartment and does not show 50 percent tumour killing. Population-specific survival and death measurements are needed; activation, recognition and killing remain distinct endpoints.
records.principle: Define added or retained populations and interaction compartments, then measure population-specific responses with appropriate controls.
strengths: Tests an immune-tumour interaction under controlled, defined conditions
Can enrich tumour-reactive T cells in a studied protocol
Can model aspects of checkpoint blockade in specialised systems
limitations: Cell proportions and phenotype can change during culture
Autologous origin alone does not establish tumour specificity
Body-level exposure, recruitment and clinical utility remain outside the culture alone

records.name: In vitro and in vivo
records.tldr: Experimental settings describe where and how a test occurs: laboratory culture, removed living material, a living organism or a computational model.
records.summary: In vitro and ex vivo describe work outside the original organism, with terminology varying by preparation and expansion. In vivo refers to work within a living organism, including animals and people; in silico refers to computation. Each setting includes different components and omits others. The label does not establish a universal ranking, human safety or treatment benefit.

links.label: Wikipedia
Source for experimental setting and intended-use interpretation
Source for experimental setting and intended-use interpretation
What exactly is 'N' in cell culture and animal experiments?
FDA: context-specific nonclinical studies and new approach methodologies

notes: Setting comparison. In vitro describes laboratory work outside the body, including grown cells and many expanded organoid assays. Ex vivo commonly describes removed living material studied outside its original organism, often briefly with retained local structure. Authors use overlapping terminology, so inspect preparation, expansion and timing. In vivo includes experiments in animals or people; identify species and host. In silico computes a prediction from data rather than directly measuring the predicted response. These terms describe where and how the experiment occurs, not a quality ranking.

Read each omitted compartment. A tumour-only dish lacks required immune interactions unless those populations are added and shown functional. A fresh slice may retain resident neighbours while losing blood flow and recruitment from circulation. A conventional PDX adds mouse circulation, exposure and metabolism without reproducing an intact human immune system. A computational prediction depends on its data, assumptions and benchmark. Human-derived tissue can be used in both dish and animal models; do not claim that ex vivo is the only setting using human tissue. A living specimen can lose cells, adapt or undergo selection after removal; retaining a structure is not retaining complete physiology. In-vitro preparations can isolate direct effects, compare doses and drugs and support repeats, while omitting perfused blood supply, host metabolism and the original population mix unless specifically reconstructed. Latin labels such as in glass, out of the living and in the living are mnemonics for setting, not quality grades.

Primary timing examples. Ladan's breast-slice assay used three-day exposures, a stated planned result window of seven to fourteen days, not a measured turnaround distribution and 23/30 usable tests from tumour-containing biopsies. Izumchenko reported 578/1,163 established PDXs and mean 16 weeks from engraftment to exposure, not biopsy to final decision. Ahlmann-Eltze compared gene-perturbation transcriptome predictions with simple baselines; the deep-learning methods did not outperform the simple linear baselines in the tested expression-prediction tasks. This was not a measured patient drug response. None of these examples shows benefit from choosing a treatment using the model. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5834154/ ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40759747/

Terminology scope. NCI's ex vivo dictionary entry describes removal, treatment and return of cells or tissue to the body. That return step distinguishes cell-engineering procedures from laboratory drug testing where the tested sample is not returned. Dosing an animal and later treating removed graft cells in a dish are different experiments. Source: https://www.cancer.gov/publications/dictionaries/cancer-terms/def/ex-vivo

Regulatory scope. FDA's roadmap to reduce animal testing concerns preclinical safety development, initially focusing on monoclonal antibodies and considering human-based laboratory and computational methods. It is not approval of every organ chip or a recommendation for personal treatment selection. Source: https://www.fda.gov/files/newsroom/published/roadmap_to_reducing_animal_testing_in_preclinical_safety_studies.pdf Decision time limits which preparation is usable: establishing a new conventional PDX generally will not fit a decision due in three weeks, while a characterised short-term assay might fit but can still fail. A treatment needing liver activation also needs the relevant metabolic setting represented; a fresh slice alone omits it. Computation can rank hypotheses without growing a model, but a universal fastest or cheapest claim is not established by the setting label.

Fictional reading exercise. Compare a graft dosed in a mouse, a fresh human slice exposed outside the body and a computed sensitivity prediction. Identify actual measurement versus prediction, host, retained cells, omitted physiology and clock before drawing an inference. These settings can start from the same tumour; days, weeks or months are illustrative scales rather than guaranteed timelines. No setting is a later validation rung of another.

An experimental setting and the origin of the material are separate descriptions. Human-derived cells can be studied in vitro, briefly ex vivo or as a graft in vivo. Living-organism work includes animals and people; it does not automatically mean a human clinical trial. Preclinical intervention experiments can continue alongside human studies, so the date relative to a first human dose alone does not validate their treatment claim.

records.name: Interferon types I, II and III
records.tldr: Interferons are signalling proteins that change how cells respond to infection, stress and immune activity. There are three families with different receptors, and a short exposure, a long exposure and a missing response can each mean something different for a tumour.
records.summary: Type I interferons (alpha and beta) share a receptor system found on many cell types. Type II (gamma) uses a different receptor system and is made mainly by activated immune cells. The type I receptor, IFNAR, is expressed on virtually all nucleated cells and the type III receptor mainly on epithelial cells (Lazear et al., 2019), and interferon gamma production is largely restricted to immune cells although its receptor is widely expressed (Schneider et al., 2014). Interferon gamma effects include upregulated antigen processing and presentation and an antiviral state (Schroder et al., 2004). Type III (lambda) signals through a distinct receptor complex, made of IFN-lambda receptor 1 and IL-10 receptor 2, that signals through the Jak-STAT pathway (Kotenko et al., 2003); in mice the response to lambda was prominent in stomach, intestine and lung, very low in the brain and spleen, and restricted to epithelial cells in kidney and brain (Sommereyns et al., 2008). Types I, II and III group interferons by receptor usage; the alpha, beta, gamma and lambda names do not measure dose or potency. Many responses run through JAK and STAT proteins and can increase antigen-processing and HLA machinery, antiviral defences, or regulatory signals; producing an interferon, receiving it and carrying out a function are separate steps.

notes: In cancer, timing and the receiving cell decide the meaning. In mice, endogenous type I interferon was required to prevent the growth of carcinogen-induced and transplanted tumours, and the critical targets were host blood-lineage cells, not the tumour cells, which differs from interferon gamma, where tumour cells are important targets (Dunn et al., 2005). Prolonged interferon signalling in experimental tumours, driven by type II and maintained by types I and II, produced a resistance programme to checkpoint blockade that was PD-L1-dependent and independent, and biomarkers of that programme associated with progression after anti-PD-1 therapy in the patient data analysed (Benci et al., 2016). In four people with metastatic melanoma whose tumours first responded to pembrolizumab and later relapsed, paired biopsies showed loss-of-function mutations in JAK1 or JAK2 in two (with no response to interferon gamma in the mutant cells) and a truncating mutation in B2M, which removes class I display, in a third (Zaretsky et al., 2016). Four patients do not give a frequency for any cancer.

Reading an interferon result needs the family, the receiver, the timing and the readout. An interferon signature in RNA is not an interferon concentration and cannot identify the producing cell. Capacity to respond under a controlled exposure is not evidence of natural exposure, and an inducible display gene score is not a count of displayed peptide complexes or a measure of tumour killing. A working display pathway can also not repair a structural loss of an HLA allele or a processing component, and stronger or longer signalling is not safer or more beneficial by default. A report on an interferon experiment should name the family, the preparation, the concentration or units, the exposure time, the cell identity and viability, and the controls, and should keep three quantities apart: a concentration in picograms per millilitre, RNA expression, and a change from a matched unstimulated condition (OnCo reporting advice). A fourfold rise in a display-gene score is not fourfold killing.

Three measurement questions need separate answers. Protein concentration in a named fluid, for example picograms per millilitre, measures amount per volume. An RNA expression or signalling-protein readout measures a sampled cellular response. Change after controlled exposure relative to a matched unstimulated condition tests response capacity in that experiment. The last result does not establish that the same exposure occurred naturally, and a fluid concentration does not identify every producer or tissue exposure. Rodero et al. (2017) measured interferon-alpha protein, interferon-stimulated gene expression and antiviral activity separately; their activity assay measured protection from viral cytopathic effects, not tumour killing.

Ayers et al. (2017) studied an interferon-gamma-related tumour RNA profile associated with response to pembrolizumab. That expression score is not an interferon protein concentration or a count of killed cells, and an association among treated patients alone does not establish treatment benefit relative to no treatment. For a controlled-exposure result, report interferon family, preparation, concentration, exposure time, cell identity, viability and controls. A low baseline score can coexist with an inducible response; intact gene sequence alone does not establish working signalling. As a measurement inference, changing an expression score from 1 to 4 relative units is a fourfold change in that readout, not evidence of fourfold killing, peptide display or matching receptor recognition.

records.name: KEYNOTE-355
records.tldr: This trial found longer survival with pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in its selected group with previously untreated advanced triple-negative breast cancer.
records.summary: KEYNOTE-355, trial NCT02819518 sponsored by Merck and published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2022, established pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy as first-line treatment for metastatic triple-negative breast cancer with PD-L1 expression. It randomised 847 patients and met its primary progression-free and overall survival endpoints in tumours with a combined positive score of ten or more, in the prespecified CPS-ten-or-more comparison. This does not prove that the effect is exactly absent in every lower-score group. OnCo links it to triple-negative breast cancer, pembrolizumab, the CPS term, the TNBC roadmap and IMpassion131. Other first-line strategies, including ADC-based regimens, are separate comparisons; this trial alone cannot rank them.

notes: In this study, previously untreated referred to the locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic setting, not to absence of every earlier cancer treatment. The 2020 report stratified randomisation by previous exposure to the same chemotherapy class in neoadjuvant or adjuvant care. The later overall-survival report met its significance criterion for combined positive score ten or more; a nonsignificant broader subgroup or an untested significance comparison does not demonstrate exactly zero effect in each lower-score stratum.

The CPS-at-least-one analysis includes people with CPS at least ten. Its nonsignificant overall-survival comparison is therefore not an isolated result for CPS one to nine. Nested subgroup findings, the prespecified testing hierarchy and individual benefit are different questions; none establishes that every person below a cutoff has exactly zero treatment effect.

Design (Lancet 2020): 847 patients randomised 2 to 1 to pembrolizumab or placebo with nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel or gemcitabine and carboplatin at 209 sites in 29 countries; the registry participant-flow table lists 35 starters across the three part-1 groups (11, 14 and 10) and 847 in the randomised part-2 groups (566 and 281), matching 882 total enrolments. Progression-free survival in CPS 10 or more 9.7 versus 5.6 months (hazard ratio 0.65); final overall survival (NEJM 2022) 23.0 versus 16.1 months in CPS 10 or more (hazard ratio 0.73, p 0.0185), 17.6 versus 16.0 in CPS 1 or more (0.86, not significant) and 17.2 versus 15.5 overall (0.89, not tested). Grade 3 to 5 treatment-related adverse events 68.1 versus 66.9 percent.

UK access: NICE TA801 (29 June 2022) limits the regimen to CPS 10 or more with immune-cell staining below 1 percent, because atezolizumab with nab-paclitaxel (TA639) is commissioned for the immune-cell-positive group.
records.setting: First-line metastatic TNBC: pembrolizumab + chemotherapy vs chemotherapy
records.replication: Consistent direction with IMpassion130 (atezolizumab, PD-L1+); IMpassion131 was negative, so the PD-L1 CPS ≥10 population and the chemotherapy partner matter. Now being superseded by ADC + pembrolizumab (ASCENT-04).

records.name: KEYNOTE-522
records.tldr: KEYNOTE-522 compared adding pembrolizumab before and after surgery with placebo on the same chemotherapy and surgery sequence in early triple-negative breast cancer. It measured improvements in response and survival.
records.summary: KEYNOTE-522 randomised 1,174 people with previously untreated stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer to a whole pembrolizumab or placebo strategy before and after surgery, with the same chemotherapy backbone. The first-602 pCR analysis reported 64.8% versus 51.2%. The 2022 report estimated three-year event-free survival at 84.5% versus 76.8%; the 2024 report estimated five-year overall survival at 86.6% versus 81.7%. An ASCO 2026 conference abstract reports seven-year EFS of 78.3% versus 69.8% and OS of 85.1% versus 77.2%. Keep each endpoint, analysis cohort and follow-up cutoff attached to its result. The trial did not separately randomise postoperative pembrolizumab or chemotherapy omission.

notes: Design (NEJM 2020): 1,174 patients with untreated stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer randomised 2 to 1 to pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo every 3 weeks with four cycles of paclitaxel and carboplatin then four of doxorubicin or epirubicin with cyclophosphamide, surgery, then nine cycles of adjuvant pembrolizumab or placebo. Pathological complete response 64.8 versus 51.2 percent (first 602 patients); event-free survival at 36 months 84.5 versus 76.8 percent (hazard ratio 0.63, NEJM 2022); overall survival at 60 months 86.6 versus 81.7 percent (p 0.002, median follow-up 75.1 months, NEJM 2024). The preplanned exploratory residual-cancer-burden analysis (Annals of Oncology 2024) reported EFS hazard ratios for RCB-0, 1, 2 and 3 of 0.70 (95% confidence interval 0.38 to 1.31), 0.92 (0.39 to 2.20), 0.52 (0.32 to 0.82) and 1.24 (0.69 to 2.23). These post-treatment strata can themselves be affected by treatment; their estimates do not separately randomise postoperative treatment or prove a benefit in every stratum.

UK sites (registry, 7): Colchester General Hospital, Barts Cancer Institute, St George's Hospital London, Maidstone Hospital, James Cook University Hospital Middlesbrough, Nottingham University Hospitals, Royal Cornwall Hospitals Truro. NICE TA851 (14 December 2022) commissions the regimen in England.
Label safety (Keytruda, 778 treated patients): serious adverse reactions 44 percent, fatal 0.9 percent, discontinuation of pembrolizumab 20 percent, most often for raised transaminases and rash.

The study question concerns the whole assigned sequence in previously untreated, non-metastatic stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer: T1c with N1 or N2, or T2 to T4 with N0 to N2, and performance status 0 or 1. The registry excludes prior checkpoint therapy and active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment in the preceding two years, among other criteria. There was one assignment of 784 people to pembrolizumab and 390 to placebo across preoperative chemotherapy, surgery and postoperative treatment, without a separate postoperative randomisation. Smaller node-negative tumours outside those entry criteria and metastatic disease are different settings. Entry did not require PD-L1 selection, and the high-risk early-stage indication in the prescribing information has no PD-L1 threshold.

The co-primary endpoints were pathological complete response at surgery, defined as ypT0/Tis ypN0, and event-free survival from randomisation. The response definition permits residual in-situ disease in the breast while excluding invasive residual cancer in breast and nodes. Event-free survival counts progression preventing definitive surgery, local or distant recurrence, a second primary cancer or death from any cause; overall survival is a secondary endpoint counting death from any cause. Because death is part of EFS, it is an event rather than a competing event for that composite. Analysing a recurrence component alone can require a different competing-risk question.

Keep the analysis cohorts separate. The 2020 first-interim pCR comparison used the first 602 randomised participants: 64.8% versus 51.2%, estimated difference 13.6 percentage points (95% confidence interval 5.4 to 21.8). The sponsor-posted first-1,002 comparison is 64.0% versus 54.7%, with a stratified difference of 9.2 points (2.8 to 15.6). That reported adjusted estimate is not simple subtraction of the rounded percentages. The current label also presents an all-1,174 pCR comparison, 63.0% versus 55.6%, estimated difference 7.5 points (1.6 to 13.4). These are different specified analysis populations, not interchangeable response claims.

At the fourth planned interim analysis reported in 2022, median follow-up was 39.1 months and all 1,174 participants contributed to the assigned-group survival comparison. Estimated 36-month EFS was 84.5% (95% confidence interval 81.7 to 86.9) versus 76.8% (72.2 to 80.7), with hazard ratio 0.63 (0.48 to 0.82). From the rounded survival estimates, the three-year absolute gain is 7.7 points, approximately eight additional people alive and event-free per 100, and number needed to treat is 1/0.077, about 13. The corresponding event risks are 15.5% versus 23.2%, a relative risk reduction of about 33%; the model's 37% lower hazard is a different measure.

The final overall-survival analysis published in 2024 used a March 22, 2024 cutoff and median follow-up of 75.1 months. Estimated 60-month OS was 86.6% versus 81.7%, with the paper reporting P=0.002; the label reports an OS hazard ratio of 0.66 (95% confidence interval 0.50 to 0.87) for the prespecified analysis. The absolute difference is 4.9 points, about five additional people alive per 100 at five years. Its reciprocal is 20.4, or 21 when rounding up to a whole-person number needed to treat. Neither this result nor the three-year EFS calculation identifies who benefits or combines benefit with harms. Comparing the 13.6-point pCR, 7.7-point EFS and 4.9-point OS gains does not show an effect shrinking over time: their endpoints, cohorts and horizons differ.

The ASCO 2026 conference abstract reports the later protocol-specified final follow-up, with an October 14, 2025 cutoff and median follow-up of 93.8 months. Seven-year EFS was 78.3% versus 69.8%, hazard ratio 0.68 (95% confidence interval 0.54 to 0.86); seven-year OS was 85.1% versus 77.2%, hazard ratio 0.64 (0.49 to 0.85). This is a conference abstract deposited by the authors, distinct from the 2024 full journal report and the sponsor-posted registry results. Longer observation of this cohort is not a second randomised trial.

Safety also retains its report and denominator. Across treatment phases, the 2020 paper reported treatment-related grade 3 or higher events in 78.0% versus 73.0%, including treatment-related deaths in 0.4% versus 0.3%. The label describes 778 versus 389 participants receiving at least one dose, distinct from the 784 versus 390 assigned. Its adverse-reaction categories and fatal-event figures must not be substituted for the paper's treatment-related categories. The prescribing information warns that immune-mediated reactions can arise after treatment stops and that hypothyroidism may require long-term hormone replacement. Event frequency, severity, duration, discontinuation and quality of life remain separate parts of the comparison.

The earlier adaptive phase 2 I-SPY2 report estimated pCR of 60% versus 22% in its triple-negative subgroup against its own chemotherapy control. That is a different comparison from KEYNOTE-522 and cannot establish a cross-trial treatment ranking. Likewise, better survival among people who achieve pCR is a prognostic association within selected response groups, not proof of the postoperative drug's separate effect or a validated rule selecting individual benefit. CTNeoBC found a strong pCR-outcome association but did not validate pCR as a trial-level surrogate for EFS or OS in its included trials. Here survival itself was measured.

The postoperative-only question remains distinct: OptimICE-pCR randomises people after pCR to postoperative pembrolizumab or observation, and the registry lists it as recruiting with no posted results. KEYNOTE-522 did not randomise dropping a chemotherapy component. CREATE-X compared postoperative capecitabine with standard postsurgical treatment after residual HER2-negative disease, while OlympiA compared olaparib with placebo in eligible high-risk germline BRCA1/2-associated HER2-negative disease after chemotherapy and local treatment. Those reports describe their own comparisons rather than a randomised test of adding either drug to the KEYNOTE-522 sequence. No result here is a personal forecast or a treatment-omission rule.
records.setting: Early-stage (II-III) TNBC: pembrolizumab + chemotherapy before surgery, pembrolizumab after
records.result: EFS HR 0.63; OS HR 0.66 (5-year); 7-year OS 85.1% vs 77.2%.
records.replication: Single pivotal trial, but the EFS and OS benefits held through the 5- and 7-year analyses; consistent with IMpassion031 (atezolizumab, pCR only) and with real-world neoadjuvant pembrolizumab series.

records.name: Laboratory certification and test authorization
records.tldr: Laboratory certification addresses the laboratory and its testing quality. Product authorization and evidence that a particular test use helps patients answer separate questions.
records.summary: The U.S. Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments program sets laboratory-quality requirements for testing human specimens. CMS distinguishes analytical oversight under that program from clinical validity, which concerns what a result means for a clinical condition. A research-use label describes intended purpose; a laboratory-developed-test description concerns how and where a test is developed and used. FDA product authorization concerns a specified product and intended use. These descriptions can coexist and do not form one universal ladder of clinical usefulness or payment.

notes: The CMS FAQ is used here for the analytical-oversight versus clinical-validity distinction, not its historical discussion of FDA authority over laboratory-developed tests. Current procedural history is retained in the separate FDA LDT-rule record.

An entry in FDA establishment registration or device listing does not itself mean that the facility or device is approved, cleared or authorized. Registration and product authorization are separate claims.

Three examples separate intended uses. Validated ER immunohistochemistry in invasive breast cancer, with appropriate tissue handling, tumour-nucleus scoring and controls, has a marker-specific pathology and endocrine-treatment assessment role; it does not validate a new RNA score as a substitute. In a wholly fictional second example, assay T version 1 detects alteration M in fixed tumour tissue under rule R, and Drug A requires exactly that result in setting S. The stipulated match supplies that requirement within the exercise, without promising benefit; another specimen, result type or setting needs evidence for the changed use. A third fictional score Q combines RNA, spatial neighbourhoods and a derived culture response to propose Drug A. Reproducibility and biological support can justify research, but do not establish that Q-guided care improves outcomes against an appropriate comparator. A laboratory certificate does not supply that missing evidence. Useful research and an established clinical use can appear on different parts of one report.

records.name: Minimal / molecular residual disease (MRD)
records.tldr: Residual disease testing looks for small amounts of disease after treatment using a specified sample and method. A negative result means no qualifying signal was detected under that test, rather than proof that no cancer remains.
records.summary: Minimal, measurable and molecular residual disease (MRD) are related terms for small amounts of disease assessed after treatment with a specified method and specimen. Blood-cancer studies can use cell-based or molecular measurements, while solid-tumour studies can look for tumour-associated features in plasma. The disease, specimen, technique, time point and threshold define the result. A negative result means no qualifying signal was detected under that method, not proof that every cancer cell is absent. Associations with recurrence, benefit from a test-guided treatment strategy, and validation of a surrogate endpoint are separate questions; evidence for one setting does not establish the others.

Powles et al.: ctDNA-guided adjuvant atezolizumab in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (IMvigor011, 2025)

notes: The name has three expansions: minimal residual disease (small remaining amounts), measurable residual disease (used in blood-cancer guidance, stressing what the method can detect) and molecular residual disease (tumour-associated molecular signals after treatment, mostly ctDNA in solid tumours). Check which one a paper means. Cell-frequency thresholds in leukaemia, molecular ratios and plasma detection rules are different quantities, and the European LeukemiaNet update on acute myeloid leukaemia sets disease-specific techniques, materials, time points and thresholds that are not transferable to a solid tumour (Heuser 2021).

Residual disease on a surgical specimen is a different measurement: residual cancer burden is a defined tissue endpoint and is not interchangeable with a blood MRD call. In a fictional study a postoperative plasma test is negative but surgery shows residual invasive cancer. Neither must be wrong, because pathology examined tissue at surgery and the plasma assay sought a qualifying signal in a later blood sample, so dates, specimen and assay limits need reconciling before the pair is read. MRD negative means a method found no qualifying signal in one specimen and not that no cancer cell remains anywhere.

A residual-disease signal can select a research group at higher observed recurrence risk without showing which treatment helps that group. Clinical utility asks whether a test-guided strategy improves a meaningful outcome against an appropriate alternative. Disappearance of a marker is a separate proposed surrogate: it needs validation against the outcome for that setting, rather than becoming proof of cure. These are interpretation distinctions in the FDA November 2024 drug-development guidance, not a universal rule to change treatment.

There is no universal MRD unit or cut-off across diseases and samples. The intended target, background and artefact controls, specimen adequacy and sampling time belong with the call; an unsuitable target or failed preparation must not silently become a negative result. A positive molecular signal does not directly demonstrate a living tumour cell, identify a lesion or guarantee recurrence. The source and the studied clinical context still need to be established.

Read an MRD report by identifying the finite specimen and collection burden first: blood, marrow or another named material. Then name the output, such as a cell percentage, molecular ratio, concentration or assay-defined call, and its disease-specific units and rules. Validation belongs to that disease, treatment setting, specimen, time point and intended decision; a threshold in one combination does not become a universal MRD cut-off.

records.name: Microsatellite instability (MSI-H) / mismatch repair deficiency (dMMR)
records.tldr: Microsatellite instability describes altered DNA repeats; mismatch-repair deficiency concerns the machinery that corrects copying errors.
records.summary: Mismatch repair normally corrects certain DNA copying errors. Defects can produce unstable short repeats, measured by defined DNA tests. Repair-protein staining examines another layer and requires appropriate controls. MSI-high, stable and indeterminate results retain their own assay definitions. Neither a tumour finding nor a retained stain alone diagnoses inherited risk, proves all repair function or guarantees treatment response.

notes: Microsatellites are short repeats; MSI is altered repeats in tumour DNA; MMR corrects some copying errors; dMMR lets repeat changes accumulate.
PCR or validated sequencing observes repeat instability; IHC observes staining for MLH1, PMS2, MSH2 and MSH6; they ask different questions and neither is a complete repair test.
MSI-H, MSS and indeterminate are assay labels; an inadequate or indeterminate specimen must keep that label rather than become MSS.
CAP recommends cancer-type-specific validation for cancers outside better-established settings and says TMB should not be used as a surrogate for MMR status.
A tumour MSI or dMMR finding does not alone diagnose Lynch syndrome; some colorectal tumours lose MLH1 by methylation.

The U.S. pembrolizumab label section 1.8 covers unresectable or metastatic MSI-H or dMMR solid tumours, as determined by an FDA-authorised test, that progressed after prior treatment with no satisfactory alternatives; this is a reason to measure accurately, not a guarantee of response.
Fictional teaching exercise: Retained IHC staining with an indeterminate DNA MSI result cannot be reported as confirmed MSS; keep both results.

DNA repeat analysis and repair-protein staining use different material and controls: extraction consumes DNA; staining consumes tissue sections. Keep the named repeat algorithm or each protein stain, adequate tumour content, controls, quality and any discordance. No universal instability fraction or staining shortcut fits all cancers; inadequate material, failed controls and degraded samples need explicit labels and review.

Colorectal cancer: 10 to 15% of resected disease but only about 5% of first-line metastatic disease (153 of 3,063; Venderbosch 2014) and 3.5% in one advanced cohort (Koopman 2009), because unstable tumours metastasise less readily. The mechanism that makes them cancers is slippage in coding microsatellites: TGFBR2 was the first such target identified (Markowitz 1995), and ACVR2A, RNF43 and B2M follow. The mechanism that makes them treatable is mutation load, a mean of 1,782 somatic mutations against 73 in proficient tumours (Le 2015).

records.name: Multi-omic integration
records.tldr: Multi-omic integration analyses measurements from different molecular layers, such as DNA, RNA and protein, side by side while keeping track of what each one measured and which specimen it came from.
records.summary: A DNA change, an RNA count and a protein or phosphorylation measurement answer different questions, so integration starts with an evidence record for each measurement: the patient or experimental unit, specimen, collection time, tissue region, method, units and quality limits. Measurements from one specimen are paired; measurements from separate cohorts are not, and even adjacent tissue sections do not hold identical cells. Three reports that copy one DNA call add no new layer, and a value predicted by a model, such as RNA imputed from an image, must stay labelled as imputed beside measured values. Multi-Omics Factor Analysis (Argelaguet and colleagues, 2018) is one research method: it infers hidden factors that capture biological and technical sources of variability, separates axes shared across data types from axes specific to one, and can impute missing data; the authors applied it to 200 samples of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia profiled for somatic mutations, RNA expression, DNA methylation and ex vivo drug response. A factor is a statistical pattern, not a mechanism or a validated test. Technical variation needs its own handling: Risso and colleagues (2014) showed that usual RNA sequencing normalisation mostly accounts for sequencing depth and fails to correct library preparation and other unwanted technical effects, and where treatment time and processing method always change together, those data alone cannot separate their effects. In a proteogenomic study of 105 genomically annotated breast cancers, 77 of which gave high-quality data, pathway analysis of the phosphoproteome identified a G-protein-coupled receptor cluster that was not readily identified at the mRNA level (Mertins and colleagues, 2016), an example of layers adding different information. Correlation between layers is not a tested dependency, and a controlled intervention addresses a different question. Layers need not agree numerically, and disagreement is not automatically an error: bulk RNA from a mixed sample can be high for a gene whose protein, on a tissue image, sits mainly in normal vessel cells, so averaging the two into one confidence score would hide whether malignant cells carry an accessible target. Combining layers can reveal agreement, competing explanations, missing evidence or a sample mismatch, and it does not by itself show that a matching treatment will help: the ESMO Scale for Clinical Actionability of molecular Targets (2018) grades alterations in six levels of clinical evidence by their implications for patient management, from targets ready for routine decisions to investigational targets that need more data (Mateo and colleagues, 2018; a second version appeared in 2026). For a prediction model, a patient who appears in several layers must stay on one side of a patient-level split, and many cells from one biopsy are not many patients.

notes: Integration card for combining molecular layers (a reading guide, not a score). Measures: relationships among named layers, not one universal multi-omic score. How: match evidence records, check quality and comparability, harmonise features, compare or model, then evaluate the stated question. Input and tissue cost: existing assay data and metadata; computation uses no extra tissue, but each original assay has its own specimen cost. Output and units: a comparison, factors, clusters or predictions, with the model version and underlying units. Thresholds: specific to the method and validated task, and none applies to every integration. Failure modes: sample swaps, cell-mixture changes, batch confounding, missing data and information leaking into evaluation. Cannot establish alone: causation, malignant-cell target location or better treatment outcomes. Validation tier: research integration gives neither its inputs nor its resulting model a clinical status.

Figure reading (fictional): the same DNA call, a T in the sequence A C T G A, is copied into Report A, Report B and Report C, which is one observation reported three times. A separate RNA assay showing a splice junction is a new measurement that answers a new question, and it does not by itself confirm the DNA call.

Figure reading (fictional Target Q): specimen S at time T1 supplies bulk RNA, where Q is abundant, and a tissue image, where Q protein is seen in normal vessel cells. Whether malignant cells carry accessible Q is unresolved, a model-imputed Q is labelled as an estimate rather than a measurement, and a different specimen or time point is not paired evidence.

Genome, transcriptome and proteome name DNA, RNA and protein collections. An omics profile measures many features within a layer, subject to its coverage and capture limits; it does not necessarily inspect every molecule. Molecular layer and spatial or cellular resolution answer different questions. Multi-omic integration relates the measured layers, with their specimen and analysis context retained, rather than turning a larger number of assays into a universal measure of certainty.

Consider an invented repair-gene R example, with measurements attributed to the same pretreatment tissue region except for a derived model. A supported splice-site DNA variant identifies a candidate sequence change. Loss of the other allelic contribution, with the variant assigned to the retained contribution, supports a possible two-hit explanation subject to copy and phase uncertainty. A reproducible abnormal RNA junction in malignant-cell-enriched material adds evidence for a changed transcript product, while reduced staining with suitable controls adds a protein-signal difference in the assigned cells. Neither establishes that every intact protein is gone. A high genomic scar adds evidence about genomic history, not a direct test of present repair. Impaired repair in a suitable model with informative cycling and damage controls addresses function under those conditions. A replicated drug response at specified exposures adds a model-sensitivity hypothesis; it still leaves achievable safe exposure and patient benefit to their appropriate evidence. These are distinct observations, not a requirement to perform every assay before using any established clinical biomarker.

A practical report reading starts with six questions: what specimen, region, date and treatment context were sampled; what object and units were measured with which assay version; whether the result is signed clinical, preliminary, research or model-predicted evidence; which controls or reference support the comparison; what remains unmeasured; and which actual decision could change. A missing field is a question to resolve, not a fact to assume. For fictional pretreatment bulk RNA, high R relative to a stated reference supports captured expression in that mixture. Calling it a surface target remains an interpretation until the contributing cells and accessible protein are established; selectivity, dependence and treatment benefit need their own evidence. Molecular layer and resolution are separate axes. Mapping 500 RNA targets in one section adds location relative to a pooled RNA result, while the measured layer remains RNA. It does not add a membrane-protein or functional measurement.

An entirely fictional core-biopsy report lists invasive carcinoma of no special type, grade 3; ER and PR below 1 percent; HER2 IHC one-plus; Ki-67 positivity of 60 percent; stromal TILs of 30 percent; PD-L1 22C3 combined positive score 15; and a supported TP53 missense finding at VAF 38 percent on a tumour-only panel. These observations retain separate rules and denominators. The diagnosis describes the sampled region; the receptor results support a triple-negative category and low HER2 staining under the stated testing rules, without establishing a particular drug benefit. Ki-67 positivity is not a treatment-selection rule here. The stromal score is an eligible-area assessment, not proof of recognition, and CPS is its own defined stain score rather than a universal immune percentage. VAF is not inherited status, cancer-cell fraction or measured variant function. KEYNOTE-355 tested pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in previously untreated advanced TNBC; its CPS-at-least-ten group had median PFS 9.7 versus 5.6 months, hazard ratio 0.65. KEYNOTE-522 enrolled high-risk early TNBC regardless of PD-L1 status. A score cannot transfer benefit between those settings. None of these invented values is a patient observation or a prescription.

records.name: Multiplex immunofluorescence
records.tldr: This approach measures several protein markers in a tissue section, in one or more imaging cycles. Image analysis then estimates cells, counts and distances under defined rules.
records.summary: Multiplex immunofluorescence measures selected protein-marker signals in a tissue section, using one or several imaging cycles. Cyclic methods build a high-plex image of one section by repeating staining, imaging and signal removal and then registering the cycles: t-CyCIF produced up to 60-plex images of formalin-fixed specimens and showed that antigenicity changes with cycle number (Lin and colleagues, 2018), and IBEX imaged more than 65 parameters in one section by iterative staining and chemical bleaching (Radtke and colleagues, 2020). A six-institution study of a six-plex PD-1 and PD-L1 panel, imaged with a locked-down image analysis algorithm, reported average intersite concordance of cell densities of R squared 0.75 in breast carcinoma and 0.72 in non-small cell lung cancer tissue microarrays (Taube and colleagues, 2021); that is reproducibility for one specified panel and workflow, not for multiplex immunofluorescence in general. A cell phenotype is a rule-based call from the measured panel, a density needs a stated denominator, and a distance needs a stated definition (cell centre or cell boundary).

notes: Assay card for multiplex immunofluorescence (a reading guide, not a score). Input and tissue cost: a compatible fixed or frozen section; staining uses material and may involve repeated processing, and the section does not preserve viable cells for a killing assay. Output and units: marker images, fluorescence intensity in assay-dependent units, cell counts, cells per square millimetre, cell fractions and defined distances in micrometres. Controls: marker-positive and marker-negative material, comparison with validated single-marker staining, channel or spectral controls, background assessment, cycle alignment and boundary overlays. Thresholds: panel-specific marker and phenotype rules locked before the intended comparison and tested for reproducibility. Failure modes: autofluorescence, overlapping signals, nonspecific antibodies, staining-order effects, tissue loss, alignment errors and incorrect cell boundaries. Cannot establish: all proteins, live-cell behaviour, antigen specificity, actual killing or universal treatment eligibility. Validation: specific to the panel, staining, imaging, analysis and intended use.

Figure reading (fictional, no cutoff): channels A and B are measured, registered marker images; the overlay adds estimated cell masks. Centre-to-centre distance includes the cell interiors, while boundary-to-boundary distance spans only the gap, so the two rulers give different numbers for the same pair. Proximity under either rule is not contact, recognition or killing.

Captures cell-to-cell proximity
Better predictor of immunotherapy response than single-marker IHC in pooled studies

records.name: Myoepithelial cells and the breast basement membrane
records.tldr: Myoepithelial cells are living cells around normal breast ducts and acini; basement membrane is separate extracellular material outside them.
records.summary: These layers help organise normal breast structures and support pathological assessment of invasion. Their location, morphology, staining controls and diagnostic context matter more than a single positive or negative marker.

links.label: Normal and tumor-derived myoepithelial cells differ in their ability to interact with luminal breast epithelial cells for polarity and basement membrane deposition.
Immunohistochemical distinction of invasive from noninvasive breast lesions: a comparative study of p63 versus calponin and smooth muscle myosin heavy chain.
Distribution of myoepithelial cells and basement membrane proteins in the normal breast and in benign and malignant breast diseases.
A spatially resolved single-cell genomic atlas of the adult human breast.
CAP invasive breast protocol: histological type and supporting assessment

notes: Typical normal breast ducts and acini have luminal epithelial cells facing the lumen, an outer living myoepithelial layer, extracellular basement membrane and then stroma. Myoepithelial cells have contractile features that help move milk; they are not the chest muscle. Basement membrane contains matrix proteins such as laminins and type IV collagen, not living cells.

Basement membrane beneath an epithelial structure differs from plasma membrane around one cell. Cell polarity describes different inward and outward organisation. Gudjonsson and colleagues' human-cell culture experiments showed that normal myoepithelial cells or laminin-1 could restore luminal orientation in collagen gels; this is model evidence about organisation, not a demonstrated cancer treatment.

Myoepithelial immunohistochemistry is supporting evidence interpreted with morphology. p63 is nuclear; calponin and smooth muscle myosin heavy chain are cytoplasmic markers. Ask which cells stain, where they stain and whether technical controls work. A failed positive control undermines an apparently absent rim.

Werling and colleagues found gaps around some noninvasive structures, stromal staining with muscle-associated markers and p63 staining in some carcinoma cells. Gusterson and colleagues found basement-membrane proteins in some invasive carcinomas. Neither marker absence nor protein presence alone proves the tissue boundary. Basal-like RNA features also do not establish myoepithelial ancestry.

In Gusterson and colleagues' 1982 tissue study, laminin and type IV collagen were detected in normal breast, benign lesions and grade I invasive carcinomas but were absent from grade II and III infiltrating carcinomas in that study. That historical cohort does not make protein presence proof of an intact noninvasive boundary, or protein absence a universal grade rule.

Werling and colleagues examined 85 breast lesions. In that series, at least focal p63 staining in tumour cells occurred in 11% of cases, while stromal myofibroblasts stained with smooth muscle myosin heavy chain in 8% and calponin in 76%. Some noninvasive structures had gaps. These assay- and cohort-specific observations explain why localisation and controls matter; they are not universal diagnostic accuracy estimates.

CAP's morphology-based histological classification and supporting-marker assessment answer a tissue question. A schematic rim is neither an immunostain result nor a diagnosis; illustrated gaps or colours cannot establish invasion. Interpret the actual tissue architecture and appropriately controlled stains together.

records.name: Next-generation sequencing (NGS)
records.tldr: Next-generation sequencing reads many prepared DNA or RNA-derived fragments in parallel, with detection limited by the chosen workflow.
records.summary: Sequencing infers base order from prepared material. Panels target selected regions; exomes primarily target exons; genomes cover coding and noncoding territory broadly. None guarantees uniform usable local evidence or analysis of every alteration class. Read length, territory, molecule independence, quality and validated use are separate features. Methylation requires an appropriate preparation and analysis rather than a sequencing category name.
