notes: Keep read counts distinct from independent molecules: paired ends and amplified copies can share a fragment. Base quality and mapping quality address different uncertainties. Usable local depth depends on explicit filters, including treatment of duplicate and overlapping reads. Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-depth.html, samtools 1.25 manual.

Fictional coverage exercise: if 900 of 1,000 target bases reach a stated 20-read criterion, breadth at that criterion is 90%. A mean of 100 reads per position does not establish adequate measurement at a particular position with four usable reads. These are teaching values, not diagnostic thresholds.
Targeted panel, exome and genome differ in intended territory; check exact coordinates and analysed change classes rather than gene count.
Exons include untranslated sequence; exome does not mean every captured base codes for protein nor that regulatory regions or rearrangement breakpoints were examined.
Ng et al. (2009) introductory scale estimates: Human genome is about 3,000 Mb; protein-coding sequence is about 1%, roughly 30 Mb across about 180,000 exons.

Zehir et al. (2017), prospective advanced-cancer cohort and computational downsampling: One hospital panel (MSK-IMPACT) covered 341 genes (2,809 tumours) then 410 (8,136 tumours) at mean 718x; downsampling to 150x exome depth would have missed at least 9% of mutations.

At a fixed budget broader territory commonly spreads reads thinner, but actual depth depends on design and usable yield; broader territory guarantees neither uniform sensitivity nor all-variant detection.
Territory labels do not specify performance for small variants, copy number or rearrangements, and conventional WGS does not automatically measure methylation.
Reduced-coverage regions exist even in clinical exome and genome workflows, including clinically relevant genes.
Fictional teaching exercise: A research genome negative at a repeat does not supersede a validated panel; a panel that never examines a fusion breakpoint cannot exclude it by a negative report.

Compare assays by accepted specimen, input consumption, designed coordinates, analysed alteration classes, local usable depth and breadth, quality filters and validated detection limits. Degradation, capture gaps and ambiguous repeats can defeat broad designs. Extraction uses material; the name panel, exome or genome supplies neither a tissue requirement nor clinical validation.

A positive control shows that the expected signal was recovered in that control under the run conditions. It does not prove that every sample call is correct. A negative sample result still needs adequate material, usable evidence at the actual position and sensitivity for the relevant alteration class. Research discovery and clinical validation for a particular specimen and use are different claims.

Lung cancer: NICE NG122 (1.2.12) says to see the National Genomics Test Directory for guidance on next-generation sequencing panels to guide treatment. In practice this is the single test that decides between tablets, immunotherapy and chemotherapy for most people with advanced non-squamous disease, which is why waiting a short time for the result is usually a better decision than starting quickly on the wrong route. The NHS explains that your hospital specialist requests the test, usually on a sample already taken.

records.name: OlympiA
records.tldr: OlympiA found better outcomes with one year of olaparib after standard treatment in people with high-risk early breast cancer, inherited BRCA1 or BRCA2 variants and HER2-negative disease.
records.summary: OlympiA, trial NCT02032823 sponsored by AstraZeneca, NRG Oncology and the Breast International Group and published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2021, showed that a year of the PARP inhibitor olaparib after standard treatment improves survival in women with germline BRCA mutations and high-risk, HER2-negative early breast cancer, about eighty percent of whom had triple-negative disease. It randomised 1,836 patients to olaparib or placebo, met its primary invasive disease-free survival endpoint and showed an overall survival benefit that was sustained at six years. It makes germline testing a treatment decision for every such patient, and whether the benefit extends to somatic or non-BRCA HRD alterations is the open question.

notes: The 2021 primary comparison randomised 1,836 people with high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer and germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants to one year of olaparib or placebo after local treatment and chemotherapy. Three-year invasive disease-free survival was 85.9% versus 77.1%, difference 8.8 points (95% confidence interval 4.5 to 13.0), with hazard ratio 0.58 and its prespecified 99.5% interval 0.41 to 0.82. In the TNBC neoadjuvant group, residual invasive disease was required; after adjuvant chemotherapy, eligibility required positive axillary nodes or an invasive primary at least 2 cm. The hormone-receptor-positive entry rules differed. The trial did not establish benefit for every inherited variant, lower-risk situation or somatic-only alteration.

The 2026 third interim report has median follow-up 6.1 years and describes maintained benefit. Six-year overall survival was 87.5% versus 83.2%, with hazard ratio 0.72 (95% confidence interval 0.56 to 0.93). The authors report an estimated survival difference of 4.4 points (0.9 to 6.7); subtracting the separately rounded percentages gives 4.3, so retain the reported estimate rather than silently treating it as rounded arithmetic. This is longer observation of OlympiA, not a second independent trial or a comparison with postoperative pembrolizumab combinations.

Second interim overall survival analysis (Annals of Oncology 2022, median follow-up 3.5 years): hazard ratio 0.68 (98.5 percent confidence interval 0.47 to 0.97, p 0.009), four-year overall survival 89.8 versus 86.4 percent, four-year invasive disease-free survival 82.7 versus 75.4 percent, distant disease-free survival 86.5 versus 79.1 percent; no new cases of acute myeloid leukaemia or myelodysplasia. Eligibility (Lynparza label): triple-negative patients needed residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, or node-positive disease or a tumour of 2 cm or more after adjuvant chemotherapy; 82 percent of the trial was triple-negative. UK: 22 registry sites; NICE TA886 (10 May 2023) commissions the year of olaparib.

records.name: Organoid
records.tldr: An organoid is a three-dimensional culture that self-organises selected tissue features. Its measured contents determine which questions it can answer.
records.summary: Organoids self-organise selected structural or functional tissue features in three-dimensional culture. Patient-derived tumour organoids are one member of this broader family, rather than complete copies of a patient. Establishment and growth conditions select cells, and identity and relevant properties need checking against the source specimen. Conventional epithelial cultures often omit immune and supporting populations; specialised retention or added co-cultures require method-specific evidence. Their use for mechanism and drug-response experiments does not by itself establish clinical utility.

Functional model interpretation: primary evidence

Dijkstra tumour identity and overgrowth checks
Sachs et al. 2018: breast-cancer organoid biobank
Geyer et al. 2023: oxygen and treatment response in PDAC organoids
DeStefanis et al. 2022: baseline size and organoid response assessment

notes: Model and assay card. Starting material may be normal tissue, tumour or stem-cell-derived material; retain its source and viable preservation method. Record malignant identity against the specimen, selected or lost populations, matrix/medium, passage and experimental window. Derivation, quality checks, expansion and testing use finite tissue and culture material. A destructive stain or lysate assay consumes its tested aliquot; recovery in another assay is method-specific. No universal specimen amount or organoid-response threshold follows from the name.

Failure and inference checks. Establishment can fail, normal epithelial cells can overgrow malignant cells, and culture conditions can select branches. Verify tumour identity rather than infer it from growth. Output belongs to the chosen assay: attributed cell counts, death-marker fraction or molecular signal, with units, time and normalisation. Check viability, composition, exposure and controls. A three-dimensional spheroid need not show tissue-like self-organisation, and specialised immune retention does not apply to all cultures. Sources: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30550791/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10598932/ Dijkstra explicitly checked tumour identity to exclude healthy-lung organoid overgrowth: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558289/

Size, matrix, oxygen supply and exposure duration belong in the experiment record because they define conditions for delivery, cell state and the readout. As a bounded example, Geyer's pancreatic organoid study found treatment-response differences between normoxia and hypoxia in specified monocultures and co-cultures. Treat size as a geometry and exposure-control question rather than assume equal supply across differently sized structures. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41420-023-01334-z

DeStefanis and colleagues tracked nearly 3,500 individual mouse-derived colon-cancer organoids. In that model, organoids at or above a change point of about 308 micrometres at baseline grew more slowly, and individual-organoid tracking was reported to be more sensitive to treatment response than well-level assessment, which averages the whole population in a well. In their 1,740 patient-derived organoids (22 lines, 19 patients) they found no relation between baseline size and growth (R squared 0.023) and no change point in any line. These are findings of one study and model, not a universal size threshold. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-022-08937-z

Fictional reading exercise. An epithelial organoid loses T cells and has lower metabolic signal after treatment. The signal does not establish immune-mediated killing. Adding immune cells creates a new experiment needing identity, persistence and specificity controls. The model can support a direct tumour-cell question while leaving host exposure, organ toxicity and patient benefit untested.

The word organoid establishes no regulatory status or clinical authorisation. Sachs's breast-cancer biobank generated characterised lines and reported retention of many source features during extended passaging; that supports a particular culture resource, not every preparation or personal treatment prediction. Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.11.010

records.name: P-value
records.tldr: The probability of a test statistic at least as extreme as observed, assuming the specified null model and all analysis assumptions. A value below 0.05 is conventionally called statistically significant. It does not give the probability that this finding is false or measure the size of a benefit.
records.summary: A small p-value means the result would be unlikely under the specified null model and analysis assumptions, but it does not measure how big or how clinically meaningful the effect is; a trivial benefit in a huge trial can have a tiny p-value while a large benefit in a small trial can miss significance. Trials with several endpoints or several interim looks must control their overall error allowance using the planned method (such as hierarchical testing or alpha spending), which is why an endpoint can be 'nominally significant' yet not count formally. The confidence interval conveys the same information about significance while also showing the size of the effect, and is generally more useful.

links.label: The ASA Statement on p -Values: Context, Process, and Purpose
ASA: official statement principles (2016)
FDA: multiple endpoints in clinical trials (2022)
OncoGuide: p-values-and-multiple-testing (pinned teaching source)

notes: A p-value is calculated for a specified null hypothesis and analysis. Assuming that null model and the other analysis assumptions are true, it is the probability of a test statistic at least as extreme as the one observed. A small value indicates poor fit to that model; it is not the probability that the hypothesis is true, that the result occurred “by chance”, or that the selected finding is false. In particular, p = 0.03 does not mean a 97% probability of benefit. Omics analyses may test thousands of genes or pathways, and reporting only the most striking result hides the search. A selected small value can generate a hypothesis without establishing a drug dependency or clinical benefit. Error control cannot repair biased measurement or an irrelevant comparison, and prespecification reduces analytical flexibility without guaranteeing a sound design.

With multiple hypotheses, the family-wise error rate is the probability of at least one false rejection in a defined family. The false discovery rate is the expected proportion of false rejections among the findings selected, conventionally zero when none are selected. They control different quantities. A confirmatory trial may allocate its error allowance across endpoints and interim analyses or use a prespecified testing sequence; exploratory analyses have a different role. Interpretation needs the complete family, hypotheses, test assumptions, one- or two-sided specification, order and chosen error-control method. Label raw and adjusted p-values and show effects and intervals beside them. Post hoc choices of outcomes, cutpoints or subgroups must remain visible.

Suppose twenty independent valid tests all have true null hypotheses and each has a 5% false-rejection probability. The chance of at least one false rejection is 1 - 0.95^20, about 64.2%. For one, five and twenty tests, this chance is about 5%, 22.6% and 64.2%, respectively. This fictional calculation concerns the whole search, not the truth probability of an individual finding. Bonferroni divides a family allowance of 0.05 by twenty, giving 0.0025 per test: p = 0.03 passes an unadjusted 0.05 threshold but fails this correction. Correlation changes the independent-tests calculation; Bonferroni control itself does not require independence when the individual tests are valid. Family definition and method choice still matter.

If fifty pathways were tested and one reported p = 0.04, a Bonferroni threshold for that family at 0.05 would be 0.05/50 = 0.001. The reported result fails that threshold; it does not prove the pathway has no biological role. The full results, planned method, effect estimate and uncertainty are needed. Missing a significance threshold can reflect low power and does not establish no effect. Conversely, a tiny p-value can accompany an effect too small to matter clinically. Equivalence and non-inferiority require their own justified margins and analyses. A diagnostic false-positive rate is a different quantity from a multiple-testing allowance. A Bayesian analysis can instead report posterior probabilities conditional on its specified model and prior. Those probabilities answer a different question from a p-value.

records.name: Examination of Low ERBB2 Protein Expression in Breast Cancer Tissue
records.tldr: In a selected 2022 breast-biopsy reader study, agreement was lower in the low-HER2 range. The reported percentages concern case-level consensus, not an individual report's probability of error.
records.summary:
Importance: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has shown efficacy in patients with breast cancer with ERBB2 immunohistochemistry (IHC) scores of 1+ or 2+ but not 0 as read in central pathology laboratories. The drug is currently being tested in large randomized clinical trials with registration intent for this patient population.

Objective: To determine the suitability of the current standard ERBB2 IHC assays to select patients with low ERBB2 positivity for treatment with T-DXd.

Design and setting: Assessment of data from College of American Pathologists surveys and assessment of analytic data from a Yale University-based study of concordance of 18 pathologists reading 170 breast cancer biopsies.

Results: The total survey data set included scores over 2 years from 1391 to 1452 laboratories of 40 ERBB2 cores from each laboratory (20 cores twice a year for a total of 80). College of American Pathologists surveys show that 19% of cases read by the laboratories generate results with less than or equal to 70% concordance for IHC ERBB2 score 0 vs 1+. When 18 pathologists read the scanned slides from a selected set of breast cancer biopsies using a 4-point scale, there was only 26% concordance between 0 and 1+ compared with 58% concordance between 2+ and 3+.

Conclusions and relevance: In this study using a current standard ERBB2 IHC assay, the scoring accuracy for ERBB2 IHC in the low range (0 and 1+) was poor. This inaccuracy in the real world could lead to misassignment of many patients for treatment with T-DXd.

Indexed on Europe PMC as PubMed record 35113160 (DOI 10.1001/jamaoncol.2021.7239). Matched by DOI alone: one bottleneck page and 17 idea pages cite this DOI among their external links (the pages are listed under Related), and this page was written so that the citation resolves inside OnCo. No figure has been checked by an editor.

records.name: The clonal and mutational evolution spectrum of primary triple-negative breast cancers
records.tldr: This study profiled 104 primary triple-negative breast cancers across several assays and found varied mutation and clonal patterns. Only a subset of validated DNA variants was observed in the compared RNA data.
records.summary:
The study profiled 104 primary TNBCs across assays: copy-number arrays in 104, RNA sequencing in 80, and genome or exome sequencing in 65. Deep re-sequencing validated 2,414 somatic single-nucleotide variants for the mutation analysis. The cancers showed a wide, continuous spectrum of genomic evolution; 36% of the validated somatic single-nucleotide variants were observed in the compared transcriptome sequence. Non-detection in those data does not establish biological silence in every cell. Basal TNBC showed more variation in clonal frequencies than non-basal TNBC. TP53, PIK3CA and PTEN mutations were clonally dominant compared with other genes, though in some tumours their frequencies were incompatible with founder status; mutations in cytoskeletal, cell-shape and motility genes occurred at lower clonal frequency, suggesting later acquisition.

The cohort is deposited as brca_bccrc (British Columbia, Nature 2012) on cBioPortal.

PubMed

findings: Coding mutation counts ranged from a handful to hundreds per tumour; 36% of the validated somatic single-nucleotide variants were observed in the compared transcriptome sequence.
TP53, PIK3CA and PTEN were clonally dominant; basal TNBC showed wider clonal variation than non-basal.
Cytoskeletal and motility gene mutations were subclonal, consistent with later acquisition.
records.whatItMeans: A triple-negative receptor label does not specify one mutation profile. Bulk sequencing and copy-aware modelling estimated differing mutation prevalences in this cohort. RNA observations add expression evidence without by themselves measuring a functioning protein, a therapeutic dependency or treatment benefit.
caveats: 104 tumours from one Canadian centre; exome depth of the era.
Clonal frequencies were estimated from bulk tissue without single-cell confirmation.

records.name: Comprehensive molecular portraits of human breast tumours
records.tldr: The Cancer Genome Atlas profiled hundreds of breast cancers on six platforms and found four main classes; the basal-like class, which is 80% triple-negative, carries TP53 mutation in 80%, frequent PTEN and RB1 loss, MYC and EGFR gains and looks molecularly like high-grade serous ovarian cancer.
records.summary:
Primary breast cancers were analysed by copy-number arrays, DNA methylation, exome sequencing (510 with matched normals), mRNA arrays, microRNA sequencing and reverse-phase protein arrays. In the analysed TCGA cohort, only TP53, PIK3CA and GATA3 were mutated in more than 10% of breast cancers. Basal-like tumours carried TP53 mutations in 80%, PIK3CA in 9%, PTEN mutation or loss in 35%, INPP4B loss in 30% and RB1 mutation or loss in 20%; PIK3CA (49%), KRAS (32%), BRAF (30%) and EGFR (23%) were amplified or gained but rarely mutated. Comparison with high-grade serous ovarian cancer showed many commonalities, indicating related aetiology and similar therapeutic opportunities. 80% of basal-like tumours were triple-negative.

Deposited as brca_tcga_pub on cBioPortal, with the 2018 PanCancer Atlas re-analysis as brca_tcga_pan_can_atlas_2018.

Basal-like breast and high-grade serous ovarian cancers share their molecular profile; 80% of basal-like tumours are triple-negative.

Associations and pathway patterns in the analysed cohort generate biological and treatment hypotheses; this profiling comparison did not test whether a drug improves outcomes in every person with triple-negative breast cancer.

records.name: PD-L1 CPS (combined positive score)
records.tldr: CPS counts eligible PD-L1-stained tumour cells, lymphocytes and macrophages per viable tumour cell. The reported score is capped at 100; assay and treatment setting determine its use.
records.summary: The combined positive score (CPS) is 100 times the number of eligible PD-L1-staining tumour cells, lymphocytes and macrophages divided by all viable tumour cells. Under the cited 22C3 TNBC method it is reported as a whole number capped at 100, even if the raw arithmetic is larger. CPS is not the percentage of tumour cells staining and is not interchangeable with tumour proportion score (TPS) or the SP142 immune-cell area score. Clinical use depends on the named assay, cancer, disease setting and treatment regimen. In advanced TNBC, the specified pembrolizumab combinations use CPS at least 10; the high-risk early-TNBC perioperative regimen has a different selection context.

notes: For the 22C3 TNBC method, count eligible stained viable invasive tumour cells and tumour-associated lymphocytes and macrophages. Divide by all viable invasive tumour cells, including unstained cells, then multiply by 100. Report a whole-number CPS capped at 100, even when raw arithmetic exceeds 100.

Tumour cells require qualifying partial or complete membrane staining. Eligible lymphocytes and macrophages may have membrane or cytoplasmic staining in tumour nests or directly associated stroma. Exclude immune cells from the denominator; do not count every stained cell on the slide. Controls and at least 100 viable tumour cells are required.

Fictional eligible counts: 200 viable tumour cells, 20 staining tumour cells, 40 staining lymphocytes and 20 staining macrophages give CPS 40. Tumour-cell-only arithmetic gives 10%, under its own assay rules. CPS, TPS and IC use different numerators or denominators and cannot share cutoffs automatically.

TPS counts viable tumour cells with qualifying partial or complete membrane staining as a percentage of viable tumour cells. Immune cells do not enter its numerator. SP142 IC scoring measures the fraction of tumour area occupied by stained tumour-infiltrating immune cells, excluding tumour-cell staining. CPS, TPS and IC thresholds cannot be transferred between methods.

For 22C3 TNBC CPS, exclude nonviable cells, neutrophils, eosinophils, plasma cells, benign epithelial cells and stromal cells. Immune cells associated only with benign structures or in-situ disease do not qualify. A CPS of 100 does not imply that all tumour cells stain.

KEYNOTE-355 randomised 847 patients with previously untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic TNBC regardless of PD-L1 status. In the CPS at least 10 subgroup, median overall survival was 23.0 months with pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy and 16.1 months with placebo plus chemotherapy; hazard ratio 0.73 (95% confidence interval 0.55 to 0.95). The CPS at least 1 comparison was not significant: hazard ratio 0.86 (0.72 to 1.04). These subgroup findings concern the tested combination and population, not pembrolizumab alone.

The US pembrolizumab label uses CPS at least 10 for locally recurrent unresectable or metastatic TNBC with chemotherapy and for first-line unresectable locally advanced or metastatic TNBC with sacituzumab govitecan. High-risk early TNBC uses pembrolizumab with chemotherapy before surgery, continued alone afterward, without a PD-L1 selection requirement. The FDA approved the sacituzumab combination in June 2026. A score does not determine individual eligibility or guarantee benefit.

IMpassion130 used SP142 IC at least 1% for the PD-L1-positive subgroup in advanced TNBC treated with atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel. Roche announced voluntary withdrawal of the US TNBC indication in August 2021. This historical regimen and cutoff are not a current US treatment indication.

In the 614-sample IMpassion130 comparison, IC at least 1% positivity was 46.4% for SP142, 74.9% for SP263 and 73.1% for 22C3. Almost all SP142-positive samples were positive by the other assays, but the reverse was not true. This was an IC comparison across assays, not evidence that 22C3 CPS and IC are interchangeable.

In a multi-institutional study, 19 pathologists assessed TNBC sections: average positivity at IC at least 1% was 58% with SP142 and 78% with SP263. Complete two-category agreement occurred in 38% and 50% of cases respectively. These study-specific results show observer variation; they do not supply a correction factor for an individual report.

A primary study of human melanocytic lesions found colocalisation of PD-L1 expression with inflammatory infiltrates and implicated interferon gamma in adaptive immune resistance. This supports a mechanism, not a universal rule that every lymphocyte-rich breast tumour has high PD-L1. Staining alone does not establish a complete immune state.

For a specified PD-L1 workflow, prepare the tissue section, stain it with acceptable controls, assess adequacy, identify the eligible cells and then apply the scoring algorithm. Further sections consume finite tissue. Record the antibody clone, platform, specimen, scoring method and intended clinical use. The cited TNBC 22C3 guide requires at least 100 viable tumour cells; that requirement belongs to the named assay, rather than to every PD-L1 method.

Report CPS as a capped score, TPS as a tumour-cell percentage, or IC as the percentage of tumour area occupied by stained immune cells. Each algorithm has its own eligibility and threshold rules. Too few eligible cells, failed controls, incorrect cell attribution, necrosis and heterogeneous sampling can invalidate or limit a result. None of these scores alone describes the complete immune state, guarantees individual benefit or establishes eligibility in a different cancer or treatment setting.

The detailed eligible-cell rules here follow Agilent's November 2020 TNBC quick guide. Its original PDF was unavailable at this check; a preserved primary-source extract supplies that historical method definition. Current treatment selection also requires the applicable current drug label and assay documentation.

Triple-negative breast cancer: the pembrolizumab threshold is 22C3 CPS 10 or more, the KEYNOTE-355 subgroup whose overall survival was 23.0 versus 16.1 months (hazard ratio 0.73); CPS 1 or more did not reach significance (Cortes 2022). CPS 10 or more was 27.2% of 232 unselected early TNBCs and CPS 1 or more 53.9% (Sigurjonsdottir 2023); 80.9% of IMpassion130 samples were CPS 1 or more (Rugo 2021). The same threshold now gates sacituzumab govitecan plus pembrolizumab (ASCENT-04). CPS 10 and SP142 IC 1% agree weakly (kappa 0.48) and are not interchangeable.

Gallbladder cancer: combined positive score was reported alongside TPS in 131 Western cases (Albrecht 2021); TOPAZ-1 and KEYNOTE-966 enrolled biliary patients regardless of PD-L1, so no CPS threshold applies to durvalumab or pembrolizumab in this cancer.

scoringRule.text: Count PD-L1-positive tumour cells, lymphocytes and macrophages; divide by the number of viable tumour cells; multiply by 100. A specimen must hold at least 100 viable tumour cells to be scored.

records.forPatient: Your report gives a CPS number. Whether it counts as positive depends on the cancer: the pembrolizumab label asks for 1 or more in head and neck, stomach, oesophageal, cervical and platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, and 10 or more in triple-negative breast cancer. The same number can open a treatment in one cancer and not in another, and a score below the cut-off does not mean immunotherapy can never be used, only that this particular indication does not apply.

records.name: Patient-derived xenografts
records.tldr: A patient-derived xenograft is patient tumour material grown in another species, commonly a mouse, for experiments under whole-animal exposure.
records.summary: A patient-derived xenograft starts with patient tumour material implanted into another species, commonly an immunodeficient mouse. It can retain relevant tumour features within a different host, while engraftment selects populations and mouse-derived support can replace human stroma and vessels. Whole-animal dosing includes mouse exposure and metabolism, not human physiology. Humanised models add selected components whose identity, compatibility and persistence need checking. Fidelity and patient prediction are question- and method-specific.

Functional model interpretation: primary evidence
PDX review: timing and selection
PDX establishment and response series
Copy-number conservation and method
NCI Patient-Derived Models Repository: identity and quality
Yang et al. 2026: specialised humanised immune-stroma model
Ben-David et al. 2017: PDX evolution
Izumchenko et al.: scoped patient and xenograft response comparisons (2017)

notes: Timing and denominators. Hidalgo's 2014 review described four to eight months to a study-ready model; it is a historical review estimate, not a laboratory guarantee. Izumchenko's series reported 578 successful grafts from 1,163 implanted specimens, described as 49 percent, and a mean 16 weeks from engraftment to drug exposure, with substantial variation. That clock is not the whole biopsy-to-decision interval. Keep submitted, established and interpretable donor models separate. Arithmetic check by OnCo: 578 divided by 1,163 is approximately 49.7 percent; the paper itself states 49 percent. Retain the counts and distinguish the reported percentage from this calculation. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4167608/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5834154/

Fidelity is measured, not assumed. Record histology, lineage and relevant molecular features against the source, host strain, site and passage, and species assignment for the mechanism. Ben-David reported mouse-specific copy-number evolution in studied datasets; Woo's direct-DNA analyses reported conservation and showed that measurement method matters. Neither establishes perfect preservation nor inevitable complete divergence for every model. Sources: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28991255/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7808565/ Engraftment is establishment of growth after implantation; passage transfers an established graft to another host. Reduced growth relative to a control is different from regression below a stated starting burden. Matching molecular features does not validate every drug prediction.

Assay card. Viable material, establishment, passage and animal experiments consume finite material. Report burden or volume with units, baseline and observation clock, exposure and comparator animals, and donor versus animal counts. Failed engraftment and excluded experiments remain visible. Human-specific binding to tumour cells does not establish activity on mouse stromal targets. A graft tested later in a dish has a different experimental setting. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3553601/

A fictional example separates denominators: ten donor specimens are submitted, four establish grafts, three yield an interpretable drug experiment and two meet its response criterion. Establishment is 4/10; response among interpretable donor models is 2/3, not a patient-response rate. A human-specific antibody binding a retained tumour receptor also does not establish binding to mouse-derived vessel targets required by a proposed mechanism.

NCI's model repository uses lineage identity, pathology and human/mouse-content checks and notes that some models evolve with passage. Its procedures and material types are repository-specific. Yang's 2026 primary abstract describes adding patient-derived tumour and mesenchymal cells, human endothelial cells and humanised marrow to a specialised immune-stroma PDX. This is evidence for a defined added-component model, not complete reconstruction of human immunity. Sources: https://dctd.cancer.gov/drug-discovery-development/reagents-materials/pdmr/models ; https://doi.org/10.1007/s00262-026-04349-4

Izumchenko and colleagues compared 129 treatments across 92 people with advanced solid tumours. Their 112/129 agreement figure (87 percent) grouped stable disease with partial and complete responses as positive disease control; reported sensitivity was 96 percent and specificity 70 percent. Requiring the exact RECIST category instead gave 91/129 agreement (71 percent). Responses came from the consulting oncologist and from xenograft volume changes converted to RECIST equivalents. These selected, repeated treatment comparisons are not 129 independent people, a head-to-head accuracy ranking against other model types or a trial showing benefit from assigning treatment by the model.
records.principle: Establish a graft, characterise source and host compartments, then compare a defined intervention using an explicit growth endpoint.
strengths: Tumour experiments under whole-animal exposure
Can assess selected source-tumour features over time
limitations: Engraftment can fail and favours some tumours: Hidalgo describes a general impression that more aggressive tumours engraft more often (for example hormone-receptor-negative more than hormone-sensitive breast tumours), so collections can over-represent them; take rate varies by tumour type
Mouse support, metabolism and immunity differ from human care
Establishment and testing can take months

records.name: Phosphorylation
records.tldr: Adding phosphate can change a protein’s behavior in several ways. The site and cellular context determine whether a measured change indicates activation, inhibition or something else.
records.summary: Protein kinases commonly transfer phosphate from ATP to a substrate, producing ADP. Protein phosphatases remove phosphate by hydrolysis without regenerating ATP. A modification can affect catalysis, binding, localization or interactions; sites on one protein can have different functions. Src experiments demonstrated an inhibitory tail-phosphorylation mechanism in their defined preparation, so phosphorylation should not be treated as universal activation.

notes: A phosphosite signal depends on modified molecules, parent-protein amount, recovery and measurement. It is not automatically site occupancy, the fraction modified at that site. A parent-normalized ratio may be informative without becoming an absolute occupancy percentage. Retain site identity/localization confidence, method, specimen handling and time.

This modifies existing molecules and is distinct from changing DNA sequence, RNA production or mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. One site alone need not identify the responsible enzyme or the state of a whole pathway.

records.name: PI3K / AKT / mTOR
records.tldr: This network links growth signals and nutrients to protein production, metabolism and recycling. Different branches can respond differently to an intervention.
records.summary:
Class I PI3K phosphorylates a membrane lipid, producing PIP3; PTEN removes its position-3 phosphate. AKT and mTOR are protein kinases. A PIP3 lipid result and an AKT1 Ser473 phosphosite result are therefore different molecular measurements. Document specimen preservation, cell mixture, protein site, timing, exposure, comparator and total-protein normalization before interpreting a change as activity or dependence.

Membrane recruitment helps organize AKT activation. PDK1 phosphorylates AKT1 Thr308, whereas the rictor-mTOR complex supplies Ser473 phosphorylation in the defined experimental route. AKT can inhibit TSC2, relieving the TSC1/2 brake on RHEB, which promotes mTORC1 signaling. The diagram's indirect AKT-to-mTORC1 connection stands for these regulatory steps; it is not direct phosphorylation of mTORC1 by AKT.

Raptor-containing mTORC1 and rictor-containing mTORC2 are distinct complexes. mTORC1 regulates protein production and autophagy-initiation machinery; releasing initiation restraint is not proof of completed recycling flux. Harrington linked S6K activity to reduced IRS-1 function, and O'Reilly observed increased IRS-1 and AKT signaling after RAD001 in cell models and treated tumors. Feedback release can change an output without proving that a combination improves outcomes in every setting.

In a fictional mTORC1 perturbation, lower production-regulator phosphorylation followed by higher AKT1 Ser473 and unchanged growth supports biochemical changes, not essentiality or failed engagement; timing alone does not prove the feedback connection. Test the proposed wiring and functional outcome independently. The FDA's 2023 capivasertib-with-fulvestrant approval specified adults with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, qualifying PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations on an approved test and specified prior endocrine treatment or early recurrence. It is not a TNBC indication inferred from a pathway label.

notes: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. PTEN, phosphatase and tensin homolog, removes a phosphate from a PI3K-generated lipid signal. These protein and lipid reactions need their own readouts. Ibrahim 2012 found that PI3K inhibition reduced BRCA1/2 expression and increased PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the BRCA-proficient triple-negative breast cancer models studied. A second branch concerns mTORC1 restraint of ULK1-associated autophagy initiation, studied by Kim 2011. Releasing an initiation brake does not establish completed cargo degradation or protective recycling. The two branches can change together without revealing the net survival effect. A model already lacking the relevant repair function cannot be assumed to gain the same vulnerability as one in which that function is newly reduced; measure protein and repair function, flux and survival under the actual compound, dose and schedule.

Rapalogs, PI3K or AKT inhibitors and ATP-site mTOR kinase inhibitors are different interventions. In Rodrik-Outmezguine's 2011 models, inhibiting both mTOR complexes initially reduced AKT Ser473 and Thr308 phosphorylation, but relief of receptor feedback later restored Thr308 phosphorylation and AKT signalling while Ser473 remained suppressed. A Ser473 result therefore did not measure all AKT activity. O'Reilly's rapalog study and Harrington's IRS feedback work likewise explain why lower mTORC1 output can coexist with increased upstream signalling. These are measured responses in specified systems, not inevitable behaviour or a universal combination prescription.

In a fictional experiment, repair RNA falls, an mTORC1-associated phosphosite falls, AKT phosphorylation rises and more autophagosomes appear. The RNA concerns messages; confirm the proposed protein and repair consequence. A validated site change concerns that output at that time, while the AKT change may fit feedback without proving every downstream effect. Autophagosome amount does not establish completed flux, and no survival conclusion has yet been supplied. Growth and energy inputs also differ: Gwinn 2008 linked AMPK phosphorylation of raptor to mTORC1 restraint during energy stress. Slower costly building work and better survival can coexist. Named S6, 4E-BP1, AKT and AMPK-target sites need their own controls, total-protein context and timing; bulk RNA is not a kinase-activity meter.
records.analogy: Think of a factory: the receptor is the order desk, PI3K and AKT are the managers relaying the order, PTEN is the accountant cancelling orders, and mTOR is the assembly line. Cancer forges orders (PIK3CA mutation) or fires the accountant (PTEN loss).
interventions: PI3Kα inhibitors (alpelisib, inavolisib) for PIK3CA-mutant HR+ breast cancer
AKT inhibitor capivasertib for PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered breast and PTEN-deficient prostate cancer

records.name: PR status (progesterone receptor by IHC)
records.tldr: PR status measures progesterone-receptor staining in tumour-cell nuclei. It is reported separately from ER and is primarily prognostic in ER-positive invasive breast cancer.
records.summary:
The progesterone receptor is an intracellular hormone-response protein. Its tissue stain does not measure circulating progesterone or every interaction with ER signalling. In invasive breast cancer, the ASCO/CAP guideline uses at least 1% positive tumour-cell nuclei for PR positivity and below 1% for negativity; ER-low positive is an ER-specific reporting category.

HR-positive is commonly used for ER-positive, PR-positive or both. Preserve the individual results: ER-positive/PR-negative is not hormone-receptor-negative or triple-negative. PR is primarily prognostic within ER-positive invasive disease. An unusual ER-negative/PR-positive combination should prompt review of the ER stain and controls, not an automatic inference about eligibility for endocrine treatment or a CDK4/6 inhibitor.

notes: PR can bind progesterone and regulate gene programmes, but finding protein in a stained nucleus is not a direct readout of all receptor activity. The ASCO/CAP guideline uses ER to predict potential endocrine benefit and describes PR chiefly as prognostic in ER-positive invasive cancer. A prognostic association and evidence of added benefit from a particular medicine are different questions.

Start with the identified tissue/lesion and invasive tumour-cell nuclei, then the validated stain, percentage, intensity, controls and final PR interpretation read beside ER. Sections are consumed by the assay. Record the specimen/block and context; preservation problems, scant assessable tumour or failed controls can limit interpretation. Percentage, intensity and composite IHC scores have different units. In-situ testing is a separate context, and no tissue-staining percentage is an individual recurrence or benefit probability.

In a fictional adequately controlled report, ER is 80% and PR is below 1%. The invasive cancer is ER-positive and PR-negative; PR does not cancel ER and the pair is not TNBC. These measurements do not alone choose a drug, quantify benefit or prescribe progesterone. Read each observation before asking the separate treatment question.

records.name: Protein
records.tldr: Proteins are amino-acid products that provide structure, catalysis, transport and signaling. A detected fragment and a complete working protein are different findings.
records.summary: Amino acids join through peptide bonds into polypeptide chains; linked amino acids are residues. Peptide and protein usage overlaps without a universal length boundary. A protein may contain one or several chains, folded domains and flexible regions. Processing, chemical modifications, localization, production and degradation affect its form and behavior. Genes specify coding templates, but a DNA or RNA finding does not measure the resulting protein’s intact structure or activity.

notes: An antibody may recognize an epitope on more than one product form or a remaining fragment. Many mass-spectrometry workflows digest proteins into peptides: a shared detected peptide cannot distinguish every full-length form. A candidate peptide sequence also does not establish its display by HLA. Separate assays address amount, location, intact form, function and antigen presentation.

records.name: RAD51 foci assay (functional HRD test)
records.tldr: RAD51 foci can inform a research assessment of current DNA repair when enough relevant tumour cells and appropriate damage and cycling controls are present.
records.summary:
RAD51 nuclear foci are assemblies of a protein involved in homologous recombination. Their interpretation depends on the sampled tumour cells, cell-cycle state, damage, staining, scoring and controls. A low count without enough informative cycling cells is uninformative rather than proof that repair is absent. The assay is a functional surrogate, not direct observation of every completed repair event.

Cruz and colleagues in 2018 assessed RAD51 with geminin as an S/G2 marker and gamma-H2AX as a damage marker in patient-derived breast cancer models and retrospective tumour specimens. Castroviejo-Bermejo and colleagues separately compared RAD51 and genomic HRD scores against olaparib response in breast cancer xenografts, then assessed feasibility in archival breast samples, including PALB2-related cancers. The latter clinical samples established feasibility, rather than a randomised benefit from choosing treatment with the assay.

A scar records accumulated genomic changes; a suitably controlled RAD51 result asks about a present repair-related state. Repair-restoring changes and acquired foci were observed in selected resistant BRCA-mutated breast cancers, but those small cohorts do not establish a universal treatment-switch rule. Use the actual assay version, informative-cell requirements and intended-use validation. A research score cannot replace the biomarker, disease and companion-test conditions of a medicine's label.

records.summary: FDA guidance on research-use-only in vitro diagnostic products concerns their intended use, labeling and distribution. The label alone is not a complete account of analytical performance or clinical usefulness, and its legal framework should not be generalized to every research model or dataset. Laboratory certification, development within a laboratory and product authorization are separate descriptions. A research result can motivate further study without becoming a validated treatment-selection report.

records.name: RNA
records.tldr: RNA is a family of molecules with several jobs. Messenger RNA provides a protein-making template; other RNAs help build, regulate or carry out cellular processes.
records.summary: RNA, short for ribonucleic acid, uses ribose and usually uracil in place of DNA’s thymine. It is often single-stranded but can fold through internal pairing. Messenger RNA carries a coding template; ribosomal RNA contributes to ribosome structure and catalysis; transfer RNA brings amino acids; regulatory RNAs influence other molecules. Many nuclear messages receive a 5-prime cap and poly(A) tail and have introns removed by splicing before translation, but these features are not universal to all RNAs. Ribosomes read a coding sequence in codons to produce a polypeptide; processing, folding and localization follow.

links.label: Wikipedia
NHGRI: RNA roles, processing and reverse transcription
NHGRI: Codon
OpenStax Biology 2e: 16-1-regulation-of-gene-expression
OpenStax Biology 2e: 16-5-eukaryotic-post-transcriptional-gene-regulation

notes: RNA abundance reflects production, processing and degradation. Short sequencing reads do not prove that a full-length intact message was captured. A noncoding RNA can function without becoming a protein, and reverse transcription copies RNA into DNA in relevant biological contexts. RNA amount does not determine a fixed protein amount or activity.

After successful delivery, a supplied ordinary mRNA can be translated at cytoplasmic ribosomes; that translation step does not require the message to enter the nucleus. Supplying a message, measuring endogenous tumor RNA and demonstrating nuclear DNA modification are separate observations. The NHGRI vaccine example illustrates supplied RNA instructions, not a general cancer-efficacy claim.

records.name: RNA sequencing & expression profiling
records.tldr: RNA sequencing measures captured RNA messages and, with a suitable library and analysis, can examine transcript joins.
records.summary: RNA normally carries and helps process cellular messages. Sequencing captures part of that RNA information through a defined preparation and analysis. Pooled abundance, transcript structure and cell origin are separate questions. A supported RNA join does not automatically establish a DNA rearrangement, functional protein or treatment benefit.

Accuracy assessment of fusion transcript detection via read-mapping and de novo fusion transcript assembly-based methods.
10x fixed RNA probe chemistry, Cell Ranger 7.2

notes: RNA abundance and RNA structure are distinct measurements. Gene-level totals can conceal splice products. Some workflows sequence synthetic probes rather than original transcript-derived material; their counts cannot establish arbitrary fusion or splice sequences. Sources: Conesa et al., methods review, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-016-0881-8; official fixed RNA profiling chemistry, https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/7.2/getting-started/cr-flex-what-is-frp.

An RNA join does not by itself establish a DNA rearrangement. Readthrough messages were observed in prostate tumour and reference samples. Authenticate independent sequence support and evaluate the genomic mechanism, protein consequence and clinical significance separately. Source: Nacu et al., 2011, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21261984/.

Splice junctions join transcript regions and many are normal; a fusion transcript has sequence from different genes; an RNA junction does not establish the DNA mechanism; neighbouring-gene readthrough occurs in tumour and reference tissue.

A split read maps across the junction; a spanning pair places two ends on opposite sides leaving the insert unsequenced; amplified copies are not independent molecules; benchmark thresholds are not clinical cutoffs.

PSI is an inclusion estimate for a defined event and denominator; local junction evidence does not reconstruct a full transcript; unfinished nuclear RNA with introns is not automatically pathological intron retention.

Whole-transcriptome, short-end counting and targeted panels recover different information; anchored multiplex PCR searches from a targeted gene end toward an unknown partner and was tested in FFPE in the original method, which does not validate later panels.
Fixed-RNA probe-ligation counts are not unrestricted fusion or splice sequence evidence.
Failure to detect a join is informative only within coverage and sensitivity; RNA support leaves DNA mechanism, protein effect and drug benefit as separate tests.
Fictional teaching exercise: A candidate A-B junction supported by three identical amplified reads cannot be called confirmed DNA rearrangement or effective target.

Use protocol-compatible RNA and record aliquot consumption, integrity, reference/transcript versions, partners, junction coordinates and independent read/molecule support. State the event denominator for splice fractions. Low expression, uncovered joins, degradation, similar sequence and preparation/assembly artefacts constrain detection. Validate support thresholds, event classes and confirmation for the exact panel and specimen; a caller name supplies no clinical validation.

Pancreatic cancer: RNA sequencing does two jobs here, calling the classical versus basal-like subtype that predicts chemotherapy response (O'Kane 2020, Rashid 2020) and catching the NRG1, ALK, NTRK, FGFR2 and RET fusions that DNA panels miss in KRAS wild-type tumours (Philip 2022).

Lung cancer: RNA is the only reliable route to the fusions with heterogeneous partners. NRG1 fusions were found in 41 of 21,858 tumours by anchored multiplex RNA sequencing with a different partner almost every time (Jonna 2019), and the founding CD74-NRG1 discovery came from transcriptome sequencing of driver-negative tumours (Fernandez-Cuesta 2014). In small-cell disease RNA is also how the four transcriptional subtypes are called (Gay 2021).

RNA adds fusions that DNA testing misses: in 67,278 patients with both, RNA plus DNA sequencing found 21 per cent more driver gene fusions than DNA alone (Gai 2025, Tempus authors). On the large approved DNA and RNA panels the FDA approval often covers only part of what is reported: the approval statement for Caris MI Cancer Seek names DNA content only, while the maker lists RNA expression and fusions as additional features.
records.principle: A common workflow reverse-transcribes RNA to complementary DNA for sequencing. Other chemistries, including probe-based counting, require their own interpretation of the captured signal.
strengths: Captured transcript abundance with defined comparison rules
Fusion and splice evidence when the library and analysis cover the join
limitations: Preparation and RNA integrity affect recovery
Bulk signal mixes cell sources
RNA evidence does not directly measure protein function

records.name: RNA splicing
records.tldr: RNA processing removes introns and joins retained exons. Different processing choices can produce different messages without changing the underlying gene sequence.
records.summary:
Splicing processes an initial RNA transcript. Exons are retained in a specified product and may contain untranslated sequence; introns are removed. For many nuclear pre-mRNAs, a spliceosome made of RNA and proteins recognizes boundary and regulatory sequences. The donor site starts an intron and the acceptor site ends it. Alternative choices yield transcript isoforms; a variant can alter exon inclusion, intron retention or use of a cryptic site. Exon skipping is not automatically a frameshift: the coding sequence and resulting joins matter. An altered message may undergo nonsense-mediated decay or produce a changed protein, but neither outcome follows from a prediction alone.

Cancer-associated splicing changes can arise through altered RNA-processing factors or their expression. SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1 and ZRSR2 illustrate studied factors; AR-V7 and BCL2L1 illustrate named transcript contexts. The linked review describes disease-specific mechanisms and therapeutic research. An altered transcript alone does not establish an intact abnormal protein, immune presentation, a therapeutic dependency or patient benefit. Free-drug development and a conjugated payload also require their own construct-specific evidence.

A junction read supports a local RNA join, not necessarily a complete isoform. Gene-level counts can hide transcript differences. RNA quality, read coverage, reference version and cell mixture affect interpretation; protein quantity and function need separate evidence.

The pathway drawing groups possible consequences studied in particular cancer systems. Its arrows do not mean that every splice change causes every listed outcome; protein formation, presentation and functional dependence require their own evidence.

Identify the reference sequence, including its version when the reference database uses versions. For an intronic change, HGVS uses a genomic reference together with the specified transcript used for coding coordinates; a mature transcript reference alone does not contain the intron. In an invented transcript whose exon ends at coding position 200, c.200+1G>A places a change one base into the following intron. The c. prefix gives coding-DNA coordinates and p. describes a protein consequence. The DNA name alone does not specify an exon skip, frameshift or remaining function; one DNA change can produce several RNA products.

In a fictional repair-gene example, a high gene-level RNA count can include abnormal splice products and messages from normal neighbours. A reproducible abnormal junction supports a local RNA join, rather than a complete transcript, its protein or its originating DNA allele. An intronic DNA base may be removed during processing, so a mature-junction read need not contain that base. Assigning the product to a particular allele needs suitable linking sequence or another justified allele-specific measurement, with cell-source and reference checks. RNA directly examines the processing product; the gene-level count cannot settle the protein-function question.
records.analogy: Splicing is like editing a recording into different versions. A changed edit can alter the final product, but the RNA join alone does not show which complete protein is made or what it does.
interventions: Spliceosome modulators (H3B-8800 negative; next generation in development)
PRMT5 inhibitors in MTAP-deleted and splicing-mutant cancers
Antisense oligonucleotides to redirect splicing (AR-V7, BCL2L1)

records.name: Single-cell mass and growth-rate assays
records.tldr: Repeated calibrated mass measurements can estimate a cell's growth rate; slower mass accumulation does not by itself show cell death.
records.summary: A suspended microchannel resonator weighs a cell relative to the fluid it displaces using the shift in a vibrating beam's frequency. Buoyant mass equals cell volume multiplied by the difference between cell and fluid density. It is not simply diameter or dry mass. Repeatedly measuring the same cell estimates mass accumulation rate; Godin reversed the flow to reintroduce the same cell to the sensor (a dynamic trap) and Cermak used serial sensors along one channel. Stevens investigated drug-response associations in specified cancer models and leukaemia samples, rather than universal clinical prediction.

links.label: Godin et al. 2010 buoyant-mass measurement
Cermak et al. 2016 serial sensors and tracking
Stevens et al. 2016 defined drug-response experiments

notes: Assay card. Input: viable cells compatible with suspension and channel handling. Record source, identity, preparation losses, fluid and temperature conditions, exposure and observation interval. Calibration maps frequency shifts to mass, often picograms. Tracking repeated readings estimates a slope, often picograms per hour; mass-normalised rates have inverse-time units. Preparation and exposure consume finite material; the physical measurement can preserve cells, but recovery and downstream compatibility depend on the method.

Quality and inference. Check clumps, cell attribution, instrument drift, calibration, tracking ambiguity and sufficient linked readings. Serial-sensor analyses exclude uncertain matches rather than invent a trajectory. Fluid-density changes can change buoyant mass. A small positive slope still indicates accumulation in the observed interval; later recovery, death and resistance need additional endpoints and time. Many measured cells from one specimen are not many independent patients. No universal rate cutoff establishes clinical sensitivity or immune recognition. Buoyant mass is also not a count of cell divisions. Physical measurement performance, a reproducible drug-response association and validated use for a clinical decision are separate kinds of evidence. Without extra measurements or assumptions, this sensor does not establish dry mass, a death mechanism, immune specificity or patient benefit.

Fictional arithmetic. A tracked cell rising from 10 to 12 picograms over one hour has a slope of 2 picograms per hour. Comparable groups at 2 and 0.5 picograms per hour differ by (2 minus 0.5) divided by 2, or 75 percent. Both rates are positive. This is a rate reduction, not shrinkage, a killed-cell fraction or patient response. These values are invented.

The positive research use is a rapid physical response readout and a view of cell-to-cell variation that a population average can conceal. Stevens measured short-term mass accumulation in specified cancer models and leukaemia samples; this can precede a large endpoint-count change, while slower accumulation can occur in living cells. A mixed specimen still requires attribution to the relevant population, and a mass sensor does not supply immune cells or recognition. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5142231/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5064867/
records.principle: Calibrate a frequency shift to buoyant mass and track repeated readings from the same cell to estimate mass accumulation rate.

records.name: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq, 10x Chromium)
records.tldr: Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing profile captured messages assigned to recovered cells or nuclei.
records.summary: RNA is distributed across cellular compartments. Whole-cell and nucleus preparations sample different material and can recover different populations. Barcodes label captured profiles rather than certifying one intact cell; quality, ambient RNA and doublet checks remain necessary. Sparse capture and selective recovery prevent a complete census, and many profiles from one biopsy do not create independent patient replicates.

In the documented fixed RNA profiling workflow, synthetic ligated probes are sequenced rather than captured-transcript complementary DNA. A barcode labels a reaction compartment and a UMI separates captured molecules from amplified copies, giving a gene-by-barcode table; a barcode does not guarantee one intact cell.

Single-nucleus sequencing samples nuclear RNA including unfinished transcripts with introns, whole cells also capture cytoplasmic messages; a mouse cortex study showed different recovery; not proof nuclei are better for tumours.
Dissociation can lose fragile cells; nuclei can come from frozen tissue; fixed-material probe methods count ligated probes and cannot reveal every variant or splice product.
A zero can be a missed molecule (dropout) rather than absence; ambient RNA contaminates profiles; a doublet combines cells or nuclei; correction does not certify every barcode.
A cluster groups similar profiles and does not prove malignancy, lineage or a clone; cancer-cell identification needs supporting evidence.
Thousands of cells from one biopsy are nested in one biological sample; splitting into two libraries does not create two patients; replicate-level aggregation is one approach.

Record compatible viable/frozen/fixed preparation, material used, chemistry, cell/nucleus recovery and quality/identity checks. Report a gene-by-barcode table with its UMI/read/probe counting unit. Cell calling, low-quality and doublet criteria are chemistry/version-specific. Selective recovery, sparse capture, ambient RNA, degradation and batch require validation; a platform name provides neither a complete census nor clinical validity.

A detection fraction uses the analysed profiles and a stated detection rule: it is not automatically the fraction of all cells in the original tissue. A profile with one immune-gene count but otherwise epithelial features is not thereby identified as an immune cell. Sparse recovery, ambient RNA and more than one contributing cell can complicate its interpretation. Check coherent marker evidence and the method of assignment; a mixture of markers does not by itself establish a new cell type. Pooling the counts from a selected set of profiles is pseudobulk. Five hundred nuclei from one biopsy can summarize that selected population, while the biopsy remains one biological specimen rather than five hundred independent patients.

Background correction estimates which part of a profile comes from free RNA in the preparation. SoupX's authors discuss deliberately overcorrecting contamination at the cost of removing a small amount of genuine signal. The estimated contamination and settings therefore need review; a corrected weak count or zero is not an infallible label of the molecule's origin.

Residual tumour here means cancer remaining in the sampled tissue after treatment. For residual-tumour research, first support malignant-cell identity, then ask which recovered states, target messages and immune profiles are present. A stress programme does not establish a genetic clone or explain survival. In Kim and colleagues' twenty-person triple-negative breast-cancer study, longitudinal exome data and single-cell DNA/RNA data in eight participants supported selection of pre-existing genotypes alongside expression reprogramming under the studied treatment. This is not a universal resistance mechanism. Compare the sampled region, time, preparation, recovery and analysis before attributing a difference to treatment; a missing cluster need not have been eliminated. In a separate fictional calculation, an input suspension truly containing 4 percent malignant nuclei gives an expectation of 240 among 6,000 retained profiles only if malignant and other nuclei have equal inclusion through recovery, capture and quality filtering. Tissue-area cellularity is a different denominator. The calculation is neither a yield forecast nor an adequacy cutoff.

records.name: Spatial transcriptomics
records.tldr: These methods measure RNA signals while keeping information about position in a tissue section. A measured spot, an estimated cell boundary and an imputed value are different kinds of evidence.
records.summary: Spatial transcriptomics measures RNA signals while retaining information about where they came from in a tissue section. Sequencing capture and imaging-based detection use different measurement units. A third approach, region-of-interest profiling such as digital spatial profiling, releases oligonucleotide tags only from regions an operator chooses; the method paper describes regions covering 1 to about 5,000 cells and panels of up to 44 proteins, or 1,412 genes with sequencing readout, on formalin-fixed tissue (Merritt and colleagues, 2020), so the result depends on how the regions were selected. The original sequencing-based method placed sections on arrays of positionally barcoded primers and kept two-dimensional position (Ståhl and colleagues, 2016); a capture spot is a positional barcode and can span several cells. MERFISH imaged 100 to 1,000 RNA species chosen by probe design (Chen and colleagues, 2015), a targeted gene set and not every transcript. Assigning molecules to cells depends on estimated cell boundaries: many methods approximate cell positions from nuclear stains, and distinguishing the boundaries of individual cells is challenging and can hamper downstream analysis; Baysor was developed to optimise boundaries from transcript composition and cell morphology (Petukhov and colleagues, 2022). Gene values imputed by aligning single-cell data to a spatial map, as Tangram does (shown in mouse brain; Biancalani and colleagues, 2021), are model outputs and not extra RNA molecules detected by the spatial assay.

notes: Assay card for spatial transcriptomics (a reading guide, not a score). Measures and how: RNA with coordinates, by preparing a section, capturing or probing RNA, sequencing or imaging, decoding, registering positions and reporting the assignment rules. Input and tissue cost: protocol-compatible frozen or fixed sections; sectioning and molecular preparation consume allocated material, some workflows alter or destroy the assayed section, and re-scoring existing data consumes no new tissue. Output and units: gene counts per spot, bin or assigned cell, and decoded molecule coordinates, often in micrometres, with physical dimensions, normalisation and observed-versus-imputed labels kept. Thresholds: assay-specific gene or probe coverage, capture and decoding quality, background and segmentation criteria; no universal high-expression or neighbourhood cutoff. Failure modes: poor RNA, incomplete probe coverage, low capture, image-registration errors, inaccurate segmentation, spillover and unsuitable reference models. Limits: no automatic single-cell identity, complete transcriptome, whole-tumour representation, proven interaction or clinical selection rule. Validation tier: many workflows are research methods, so check analytical and intended-use validation for the exact assay and model; resolution claims and regulatory status are separate questions.

Figure reading (fictional geometry, no platform scale): a capture spot is one barcode that can pool several cells. Imaging decodes six RNA coordinates, three for gene G and three for gene H (3 + 3 = 6), and these are coordinates, not cell labels. Moving the estimated cell masks changes which cell a coordinate is assigned to while the RNA stays fixed. Gene R is absent from the G and H panel, so a model-inferred R value is not an observed molecule, and RNA position is not protein or function.

In a fictional map, each of two regions contains twelve illustrative immune cells, but one places them within malignant nests and the other outside. Equal cell symbols do not guarantee equal bulk RNA: similar RNA is a separately stipulated condition of the example. The map supplies neither a stromal-area TIL score nor evidence of recognition or treatment benefit. A capture spot can pool several cells, and changing an estimated cell boundary can change molecule assignment while the observed RNA coordinates stay fixed.

records.name: T-cell receptor
records.tldr: A conventional T-cell receptor recognises a peptide together with its HLA display. Recognition alone does not show killing.
records.summary:
A conventional alpha-beta T-cell receptor uses paired chains to recognise a peptide-HLA surface. Its recognition chains assemble with CD3 signalling partners, as demonstrated in the human TCR-CD3 structural study. CDR3 is an informative variable region, but neither a beta-chain sequence nor CDR3 alone specifies the complete paired receptor or its function.

Particular receptors can cross-react across peptide and HLA contexts; that does not establish a universal cross-reactivity rate. Paired receptor identity, binding, activation, target-cell death and clinical benefit require different evidence. A response by one reconstructed pair to peptide-loaded cells does not establish that another alpha-chain pairing recognises the same target, or that either kills naturally presenting tumour cells. Use irrelevant-target, HLA and target-only viability controls. Peptide loading can bypass natural processing, and contact diagrams are not healthy-tissue safety tests.

notes: A conventional alpha-beta TCR uses paired variable and constant domains to contact peptide plus HLA. The peptide sits in the HLA groove, not a separate TCR peptide pocket. CD3 signalling partners are distinct from recognition chains. Contact loops including junction-spanning CDR3 contribute, but other loops, the partner chain and HLA matter; beta-only or CDR3-only sequence is incomplete.

Cross-reactivity is recognition of multiple targets by a receptor. Defined receptor experiments demonstrated peptide/HLA cross-reactivity, not recognition of every allele by an arbitrary receptor or a universal rate. Greater affinity or a contact drawing does not establish healthy-tissue safety.

Sequencing reports sampled receptor identities and abundances under an operational clonotype definition. Paired alpha-beta identities are more complete than beta alone. Peptide-HLA multimer binding, stimulus-induced cellular response, target-cell death and clinical benefit are different endpoints. Include irrelevant-target, HLA and target-only viability controls; peptide-loaded cells can bypass natural processing.

Vaccination generally recruits or expands existing mature receptor specificities rather than rewriting each mature receptor. Engineered TCR therapy introduces selected receptor sequences. In either case, tested recognition must still connect to naturally presenting tumour targets, useful function and healthy-tissue safety. If one beta sequence pairs with different alpha chains, a positive reconstruction of one pair does not establish the other pair's function or tumour killing.

Source scope: teaching synthesis checked against the cited abstracts and specified accessible primary text on 9 November 2026; fictional examples are not clinical observations or treatment-selection rules.

Many measured conventional receptor-peptide-HLA interactions have micromolar dissociation constants; affinity, multiple contacts, CD4/CD8 coreceptors and the cellular signalling context contribute differently to activity. Stone and colleagues review those distinctions, rather than a universal affinity ranking against every antibody. One receptor type per cell is also a simplification: extra productive alpha chains and dual surface receptors have been documented. A chain sequence alone does not establish which assembled receptor provides the measured specificity.

records.name: Ducts, lobules and the terminal duct lobular unit
records.tldr: Breast ducts connect to milk-producing acini, with supporting tissues around them. This anatomy helps interpret a sample but does not by itself establish cancer.
records.summary:
The breast contains an interconnected duct-lobular epithelial system within connective and fatty tissue. A terminal duct with its associated acini forms a terminal duct lobular unit. Tissue compartments and their proportions matter when interpreting imaging, microscopy or bulk molecular measurements. Histological diagnosis, grade, receptor status and disease extent require their own evidence.

NCI DCEG describes the TDLU as the origin of most breast cancer precursors and cancers. The names ductal and lobular are diagnostic morphology, not proof of an exact ancestral cell. Characteristic loss of E-cadherin in invasive lobular carcinoma reduces cell adhesion; diffuse growth in unconnected lines can make a lesion harder to feel or detect on imaging. The SEER description concerns this growth pattern rather than a universal test result for every lobular tumour.

Male breasts have ducts and may have lobules, but far fewer than female breasts; NCI describes lobular cancer as rare in men. Breast tissue and mammographic density change over life. Greater density is associated with higher breast-cancer risk and can obscure cancers on a mammogram; increasing age and childbearing are associated with lower density, alongside other influences. Mammographic density, TDLU involution and histological diagnosis are different observations.
